89# Flush-time batching limits shared by the PostgreSQL non-graph write paths 

90# (PGKVStorage, PGVectorStorage, PGDocStatusStorage). Mirrors the MONGO_* / 

91# OPENSEARCH_* contract: the payload-byte budget is the primary limiter and the 

92# record-count caps are a secondary guard. Unlike Mongo/OpenSearch there is no 

93# single server-side bulk message to stay under -- asyncpg's executemany 

94# pipelines each row over a reused prepared statement -- so for PostgreSQL the 

95# byte budget mainly bounds client-side peak memory and transaction duration. 

96# The default record cap keeps PGKVStorage's historical 200 behaviour; delete 

97# ids are short strings so a larger count cap is safe. 

98DEFAULT_PG_UPSERT_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024 # 16 MiB 

99DEFAULT_PG_UPSERT_MAX_RECORDS_PER_BATCH = 200 

100DEFAULT_PG_DELETE_MAX_RECORDS_PER_BATCH = 1000 

101

105# something we cannot use", and let the former reach _run_with_retry unwrapped.

111 asyncpg.exceptions.InterfaceError, 

112 asyncpg.exceptions.TooManyConnectionsError,

119# First Apache AGE version whose graph queries can crash the PostgreSQL backend from 

120# PGGraphStorage. Deliberately an upper bound rather than a blocklist of known-bad 

121# points: a later AGE release is only safe once someone has verified it, and letting 

122# unverified versions through would defeat the check. Raise this only with evidence. 

123# See https://github.com/apache/age/issues/2500. 

124AGE_FIRST_UNSUPPORTED_VERSION = (1, 8, 0) 

125AGE_ALLOW_UNSUPPORTED_ENV = "POSTGRES_AGE_ALLOW_UNSUPPORTED_VERSION" 

126 

127# Both sources are consulted, because neither alone sees every affected deployment. 

128# pg_extension.extversion is the version of the SQL script that was last run against 

129# this database, so it does not move when the binaries are swapped underneath it: 

130# starting 1.8.0 binaries over a data directory created under 1.7.0 leaves it at 

131# '1.7.0' while the 1.8.0 age.so is what actually executes. default_version comes from 

132# the on-disk age.control and therefore tracks the binaries. 

133# 

134# Two independent lookups rather than one join, because the two catalogs do not fail 

135# alike. pg_extension is an ordinary catalog table. pg_available_extensions is a view 

136# that parses every control file in the sharedir, so one malformed file belonging to an 

137# unrelated extension makes the whole view raise -- and that says nothing about AGE, so 

138# it must not be able to refuse startup on a server that has no AGE at all. Read apart, 

139# each source can be missing or unreadable on its own, and "neither catalog names age" 

140# -- the only state where there is genuinely nothing to gate -- means both lookups 

141# returned None *and* both actually answered: a lookup that failed is not a lookup that 

142# found nothing. default_version is itself NULLABLE, so the available lookup is read with 

143# fetchrow rather than fetchval -- a row naming 'age' with a NULL version is an age.control 

144# that is on disk, which is the opposite of the absence a bare None would suggest. 

145# The asymmetry in how these two are read is load-bearing, not an oversight to tidy up: 

146# the installed lookup may use fetchval only because pg_extension.extversion is 

147# text NOT NULL, so "no row" and "NULL value" cannot both occur there. Giving the 

148# available lookup the same treatment would reopen the bug the paragraph above describes. 

149AGE_INSTALLED_SQL = "SELECT extversion FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'age'" 

150AGE_AVAILABLE_SQL = ( 

151 "SELECT default_version FROM pg_available_extensions WHERE name = 'age'" 

152) 

153 

154 

155# Distinguishes "this source said nothing" from "this source said something we cannot 

156# read". Both used to collapse to None, which let an unreadable source be ignored while 

157# its sibling decided alone -- exactly the in-place-upgrade hole the second source exists 

158# to close. A named type rather than a bare object() so that the return annotation below 

159# stays narrower than `object`, and a type checker can still catch a caller that treats 

160# the sentinel as a version. 

161class _AgeVersionUnparseable: 

162 """Singleton marker: the source is present but not a version we understand.""" 

163 

164 

165_AGE_VERSION_UNPARSEABLE = _AgeVersionUnparseable() 

166 

167# Exactly three ASCII numeric components. Signs, PEP-515 underscores and non-ASCII 

168# digits are all accepted by int() but are not things AGE reports, and short forms are 

169# deliberately no longer padded to three: a value we had to repair before comparing it 

170# is not a value we read, and per AGE_FIRST_UNSUPPORTED_VERSION anything we have not 

171# verified must not reach the safe side of the comparison. 

172_AGE_VERSION_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+") 

173 

174 

175def _parse_age_version( 

176 raw: Any, 

177) -> tuple[int, int, int] | _AgeVersionUnparseable | None: 

178 """Parse an Apache AGE version string into a comparable tuple. 

179 

180 Returns None only if the source is absent (``raw is None``), so that a source this 

181 deployment simply does not have cannot stop the other from deciding. Returns 

182 ``_AGE_VERSION_UNPARSEABLE`` if the source is present but is not a version we 

183 understand -- including present-but-blank: that is an *unverified* version, not a 

184 silent one, and by the policy stated on AGE_FIRST_UNSUPPORTED_VERSION an unverified 

185 version must not be let through. An unrecognised value is reported through that 

186 return value rather than as an exception; the caller decides. 

187 """ 

188 if raw is None: 

189 return None 

190 raw_str = str(raw) 

191 if not _AGE_VERSION_RE.fullmatch(raw_str): 

192 return _AGE_VERSION_UNPARSEABLE 

193 major, minor, patch = (int(p) for p in raw_str.split(".")) 

194 return (major, minor, patch)

197def _estimate_record_bytes(record: tuple[Any, ...]) -> int: 

198 """Estimate the serialized byte size of one asyncpg parameter tuple. 

199 

200 A splitting *heuristic* for ``_chunk_by_budget``, not the exact wire size. 

201 numpy vectors dominate vector rows and large text dominates KV rows, so the 

202 estimate sums those accurately and treats scalars as a small constant: 

203 

204 * ``np.ndarray`` -> ``.nbytes`` (the binary pgvector payload) 

205 * ``str`` -> UTF-8 byte length 

206 * ``bytes`` / ``bytearray`` -> ``len`` 

207 * ``dict`` / ``list`` -> compact-JSON UTF-8 length (already-serialized 

208 JSON columns are passed as ``str`` and handled above; this covers any 

209 not-yet-serialized field) 

210 * ``None`` -> 0 

211 * everything else (int / float / datetime / ...) -> a small constant 

212 """ 

213 total = 0 

214 for field_value in record: 

215 if isinstance(field_value, np.ndarray): 

216 total += field_value.nbytes 

217 elif isinstance(field_value, str): 

218 total += len(field_value.encode("utf-8")) 

219 elif isinstance(field_value, (bytes, bytearray)): 

220 total += len(field_value) 

221 elif field_value is None: 

222 total += 0 

223 elif isinstance(field_value, (dict, list)): 

224 total += len( 

225 json.dumps( 

226 field_value, 

227 ensure_ascii=False, 

228 separators=(",", ":"), 

229 default=str, 

230 ).encode("utf-8") 

231 ) 

232 else: 

233 total += 16 

234 return total 

235

237def _chunk_by_budget( 

238 items: list[T], 

239 size_of: Callable[[T], int], 

240 max_payload_bytes: int, 

241 max_records_per_batch: int, 

242) -> list[tuple[list[T], int]]: 

243 """Split items into batches by estimated payload size (primary) and count. 

244 

245 The byte budget is the primary limiter: items accumulate until adding the 

246 next one would exceed ``max_payload_bytes``, then a new batch starts. 

247 ``size_of(item)`` returns an item's estimated serialized byte size. A single 

248 item larger than the byte budget is emitted as its own batch rather than 

249 raising; the server stays the final arbiter. A non-positive limit disables 

250 that dimension. Returns ``(batch, summed_estimated_bytes)`` tuples (the 

251 estimate is used for logging). Semantically identical to mongo_impl's 

252 ``_chunk_by_budget``. 

253 """ 

254 if not items: 

255 return [] 

256 

257 payload_limit = max_payload_bytes if max_payload_bytes > 0 else float("inf") 

258 records_limit = max_records_per_batch if max_records_per_batch > 0 else float("inf") 

259 

260 batches: list[tuple[list[T], int]] = [] 

261 current: list[T] = [] 

262 # JSON array overhead ("[]") 

263 current_bytes = 2 

264 

265 for item in items: 

266 item_bytes = size_of(item) 

267 # If current batch not empty, a comma is needed before next element. 

268 separator_overhead = 1 if current else 0 

269 next_bytes = current_bytes + separator_overhead + item_bytes 

270 

271 if current and (len(current) >= records_limit or next_bytes > payload_limit): 

272 batches.append((current, current_bytes)) 

273 current = [] 

274 current_bytes = 2 

275 next_bytes = current_bytes + item_bytes 

276 

277 current.append(item) 

278 current_bytes = next_bytes 

279 

280 if current: 280 ↛ 283line 280 didn't jump to line 283 because the condition on line 280 was always true

281 batches.append((current, current_bytes)) 

282 

283 return batches 

284

286def _resolve_pg_batch_limits() -> tuple[int, int, int]: 

287 """Resolve flush-time batching limits from env, with module defaults. 

288 

289 Shared by every PostgreSQL non-graph write path so the byte/record caps that 

290 bound a single ``executemany`` / ``DELETE ... ANY($2)`` are consistent across 

291 all of them. A non-positive value disables that splitting dimension and logs 

292 a warning. Returns ``(upsert_payload_bytes, upsert_records, delete_records)``. 

293 """ 

294 upsert_payload_bytes = int( 

295 os.environ.get( 

296 "POSTGRES_UPSERT_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES", 

297 str(DEFAULT_PG_UPSERT_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES), 

298 ) 

299 ) 

300 upsert_records = int( 

301 os.environ.get( 

302 "POSTGRES_UPSERT_MAX_RECORDS_PER_BATCH", 

303 str(DEFAULT_PG_UPSERT_MAX_RECORDS_PER_BATCH), 

304 ) 

305 ) 

306 delete_records = int( 

307 os.environ.get( 

308 "POSTGRES_DELETE_MAX_RECORDS_PER_BATCH", 

309 str(DEFAULT_PG_DELETE_MAX_RECORDS_PER_BATCH), 

310 ) 

311 ) 

312 if upsert_payload_bytes <= 0: 

313 logger.warning( 

314 f"POSTGRES_UPSERT_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES={upsert_payload_bytes} is non-positive, disable payload-size splitting" 

315 ) 

316 if upsert_records <= 0: 

317 logger.warning( 

318 f"POSTGRES_UPSERT_MAX_RECORDS_PER_BATCH={upsert_records} is non-positive, disable upsert record-count splitting" 

319 ) 

320 if delete_records <= 0: 

321 logger.warning( 

322 f"POSTGRES_DELETE_MAX_RECORDS_PER_BATCH={delete_records} is non-positive, disable delete record-count splitting" 

323 ) 

324 return upsert_payload_bytes, upsert_records, delete_records

336def _safe_index_name(table_name: str, index_suffix: str) -> str: 

337 """ 

338 Generate a PostgreSQL-safe index name that won't be truncated. 

339 

340 PostgreSQL silently truncates identifiers to 63 bytes. This function 

341 ensures index names stay within that limit by hashing long table names. 

342 

343 Args: 

344 table_name: The table name (may be long with model suffix) 

345 index_suffix: The index type suffix (e.g., 'hnsw_cosine', 'id', 'workspace_id') 

346 

347 Returns: 

348 A deterministic index name that fits within 63 bytes 

349 """ 

350 # Construct the full index name 

351 full_name = f"idx_{table_name.lower()}_{index_suffix}" 

352 

353 # If it fits within the limit, use it as-is 

354 if len(full_name.encode("utf-8")) <= PG_MAX_IDENTIFIER_LENGTH: 

355 return full_name 

356 

357 # Otherwise, hash the table name to create a shorter unique identifier 

358 # Keep 'idx_' prefix and suffix readable, hash the middle 

359 hash_input = table_name.lower().encode("utf-8") 

360 table_hash = hashlib.md5(hash_input).hexdigest()[:12] # 12 hex chars 

361 

362 # Format: idx_{hash}_{suffix} - guaranteed to fit 

363 # Maximum: idx_ (4) + hash (12) + _ (1) + suffix (variable) = 17 + suffix 

364 shortened_name = f"idx_{table_hash}_{index_suffix}" 

365 

366 return shortened_name

374def _dollar_quote(s: str, tag_prefix: str = "AGE") -> str: 

375 """ 

376 Generate a PostgreSQL dollar-quoted string with a unique tag. 

377 

378 PostgreSQL dollar-quoting uses $tag$ as delimiters. If the content contains 

379 the same delimiter (e.g., $$ or $AGE1$), it will break the query. 

380 This function finds a unique tag that doesn't conflict with the content. 

381 

382 Args: 

383 s: The string to quote 

384 tag_prefix: Prefix for generating unique tags (default: "AGE") 

385 

386 Returns: 

387 The dollar-quoted string with a unique tag, e.g., $AGE1$content$AGE1$ 

388 

389 Example: 

390 >>> _dollar_quote("hello") 

391 '$AGE1$hello$AGE1$' 

392 >>> _dollar_quote("$AGE1$ test") 

393 '$AGE2$$AGE1$ test$AGE2$' 

394 >>> _dollar_quote("$$$") # Content with dollar signs 

395 '$AGE1$$$$$AGE1$' 

396 >>> _dollar_quote("ends with $AGE1") # tail would merge with the tag 

397 '$AGE2$ends with $AGE1$AGE2$' 

398 """ 

399 s = "" if s is None else str(s) 

400 for i in itertools.count(1): 400 ↛ exitline 400 didn't return from function '_dollar_quote' because the loop on line 400 didn't complete

401 tag = f"{tag_prefix}{i}" 

402 wrapper = f"${tag}$" 

403 # `wrapper not in s` alone is not enough. The delimiter `$tag$` has a 

404 # one-character border ("$" is both its first and last char), so when 

405 # `s` ends with `$tag` (i.e. `wrapper` minus its trailing "$"), the 

406 # leading "$" of the appended closing wrapper completes a premature 

407 # `$tag$` at the seam, truncating the literal and leaking the rest as 

408 # raw SQL. Reject such a tag so the chosen delimiter cannot form across 

409 # the content/closing boundary either. See test_dollar_quote_*. 

410 if wrapper not in s and not s.endswith(wrapper[:-1]): 

411 return f"{wrapper}{s}{wrapper}" 

412 

413 

414# PostgreSQL's `name` type (NAMEDATALEN - 1). Graph and label names are stored 

415# as `name`, so anything longer is clipped on the way in and lookups have to 

416# clip the value they compare against. 

417_PG_NAME_MAX_BYTES = 63

490 def _create_ssl_context(self) -> ssl.SSLContext | None: 

491 """Create SSL context based on configuration parameters.""" 

492 if not self.ssl_mode: 

493 return None 

494 

495 ssl_mode = self.ssl_mode.lower() 

496 

497 # For simple modes that don't require custom context 

498 if ssl_mode in ["disable", "allow", "prefer", "require"]: 

499 if ssl_mode == "disable": 

500 return None 

501 elif ssl_mode in ["require", "prefer", "allow"]: 

502 # Return None for simple SSL requirement, handled in initdb 

503 return None 

504 

505 # For modes that require certificate verification 

506 if ssl_mode in ["verify-ca", "verify-full"]: 

507 try: 

508 context = ssl.create_default_context(ssl.Purpose.SERVER_AUTH) 

509 

510 # Configure certificate verification 

511 if ssl_mode == "verify-ca": 

512 context.check_hostname = False 

513 elif ssl_mode == "verify-full": 

514 context.check_hostname = True 

515 

516 # Load root certificate if provided 

517 if self.ssl_root_cert: 

518 if os.path.exists(self.ssl_root_cert): 

519 context.load_verify_locations(cafile=self.ssl_root_cert) 

520 logger.info( 

521 f"PostgreSQL, Loaded SSL root certificate: {self.ssl_root_cert}" 

522 ) 

523 else: 

524 logger.warning( 

525 f"PostgreSQL, SSL root certificate file not found: {self.ssl_root_cert}" 

526 ) 

527 

528 # Load client certificate and key if provided 

529 if self.ssl_cert and self.ssl_key: 

530 if os.path.exists(self.ssl_cert) and os.path.exists(self.ssl_key): 

531 context.load_cert_chain(self.ssl_cert, self.ssl_key) 

532 logger.info( 

533 f"PostgreSQL, Loaded SSL client certificate: {self.ssl_cert}" 

534 ) 

535 else: 

536 logger.warning( 

537 "PostgreSQL, SSL client certificate or key file not found" 

538 ) 

539 

540 # Load certificate revocation list if provided 

541 if self.ssl_crl: 

542 if os.path.exists(self.ssl_crl): 

543 context.load_verify_locations(crlfile=self.ssl_crl) 

544 logger.info(f"PostgreSQL, Loaded SSL CRL: {self.ssl_crl}") 

545 else: 

546 logger.warning( 

547 f"PostgreSQL, SSL CRL file not found: {self.ssl_crl}" 

548 ) 

549 

550 return context 

551 

552 except Exception as e: 

553 logger.error(f"PostgreSQL, Failed to create SSL context: {e}") 

554 raise ValueError(f"SSL configuration error: {e}") 

555 

556 # Unknown SSL mode 

557 logger.warning(f"PostgreSQL, Unknown SSL mode: {ssl_mode}, SSL disabled") 

558 return None

561 # Prepare connection parameters 

562 connection_params = { 

563 "user": self.user, 

564 "password": self.password, 

565 "database": self.database, 

566 "host": self.host, 

567 "port": self.port, 

568 "min_size": 1, 

569 "max_size": self.max, 

570 } 

571 

572 # Only add statement_cache_size if it's configured 

573 if self.statement_cache_size is not None: 

574 connection_params["statement_cache_size"] = int(self.statement_cache_size) 

575 logger.info( 

576 f"PostgreSQL, statement LRU cache size set as: {self.statement_cache_size}" 

577 ) 

578 

579 # Add SSL configuration if provided 

580 ssl_context = self._create_ssl_context() 

581 if ssl_context is not None: 

582 connection_params["ssl"] = ssl_context 

583 logger.info("PostgreSQL, SSL configuration applied") 

584 elif self.ssl_mode: 

585 # Handle simple SSL modes without custom context 

586 if self.ssl_mode.lower() in ["require", "prefer"]: 

587 connection_params["ssl"] = True 

588 elif self.ssl_mode.lower() == "disable": 

589 connection_params["ssl"] = False 

590 logger.info(f"PostgreSQL, SSL mode set to: {self.ssl_mode}") 

591 

592 # Add server settings if provided 

593 if self.server_settings: 

594 try: 

595 settings = {} 

596 # The format is expected to be a query string, e.g., "key1=value1&key2=value2" 

597 pairs = self.server_settings.split("&") 

598 for pair in pairs: 

599 if "=" in pair: 

600 key, value = pair.split("=", 1) 

601 settings[key] = value 

602 if settings: 

603 connection_params["server_settings"] = settings 

604 logger.info(f"PostgreSQL, Server settings applied: {settings}") 

605 except Exception as e: 

606 logger.warning( 

607 f"PostgreSQL, Failed to parse server_settings: {self.server_settings}, error: {e}" 

608 ) 

609 

610 wait_strategy = ( 

611 wait_exponential( 

612 multiplier=self.connection_retry_backoff, 

613 min=self.connection_retry_backoff, 

614 max=self.connection_retry_backoff_max, 

615 ) 

616 if self.connection_retry_backoff > 0 

617 else wait_fixed(0) 

618 ) 

619 

620 async def _init_connection(connection: asyncpg.Connection) -> None: 

621 """Initialize each new connection with pgvector codec and VCHORDRQ session params. 

622 

623 Called once per physical connection creation (not on pool reuse). 

624 register_vector is a Python-level codec registration that survives 

625 asyncpg's RESET ALL; VCHORDRQ GUCs do not — they are re-applied in 

626 _reset_connection after each pool release. 

627 """ 

628 if self.enable_vector: 

629 if not pm.is_installed("pgvector"): 

630 pm.install("pgvector") 

631 from pgvector.asyncpg import register_vector # type: ignore 

632 

633 await register_vector(connection) 

634 if self.enable_vector and self.vector_index_type == "VCHORDRQ": 

635 await self.configure_vchordrq(connection) 

636 

637 async def _reset_connection(connection: asyncpg.Connection) -> None: 

638 """Run the default asyncpg cleanup, then re-apply VCHORDRQ session GUCs. 

639 

640 When a custom reset= callback is registered with create_pool(), asyncpg 

641 calls Connection._reset() (private — clears listeners and rolls back open 

642 transactions if any) and then this function. It does NOT call the public 

643 Connection.reset(), which is the method that calls _reset() and then 

644 executes the cleanup query returned by get_reset_query() — the exact SQL 

645 depends on detected server capabilities and typically includes 

646 pg_advisory_unlock_all(), CLOSE ALL, UNLISTEN *, and RESET ALL. 

647 

648 We must therefore run that cleanup ourselves via get_reset_query() before 

649 restoring VCHORDRQ GUCs. Skipping this step leaks session state across 

650 pool checkouts — for example configure_age() sets search_path and that 

651 modified path would persist into the next non-AGE connection checkout. 

652 

653 register_vector is NOT repeated here: it is a Python-side encoder/decoder 

654 registration on the asyncpg Connection object and is unaffected by RESET ALL. 

655 Note that set_type_codec() clears the statement cache, which is naturally 

656 repopulated on subsequent queries. 

657 """ 

658 try: 

659 # Run the default cleanup that asyncpg would otherwise handle. 

660 reset_query = connection.get_reset_query() 

661 if reset_query: 

662 await connection.execute(reset_query) 

663 except Exception as e: 

664 logger.error( 

665 f"[{self.workspace}] Pool reset cleanup query failed — connection " 

666 f"will be terminated and removed from pool: {e}" 

667 ) 

668 raise 

669 

670 # RESET ALL clears session GUCs; restore VCHORDRQ values afterward. 

671 if self.enable_vector and self.vector_index_type == "VCHORDRQ": 

672 try: 

673 await self.configure_vchordrq(connection) 

674 except asyncpg.exceptions.UndefinedObjectError: 

675 logger.error( 

676 f"[{self.workspace}] VCHORDRQ extension is not installed. " 

677 "Install the extension or set vector_index_type to a supported value. " 

678 "Connection will be terminated and removed from pool." 

679 ) 

680 raise 

681 except asyncpg.exceptions.InvalidParameterValueError as e: 

682 logger.error( 

683 f"[{self.workspace}] Invalid VCHORDRQ GUC parameter — " 

684 f"check vchordrq_probes and vchordrq_epsilon config. " 

685 f"Connection will be terminated: {e}" 

686 ) 

687 raise 

688 except Exception as e: 

689 logger.error( 

690 f"[{self.workspace}] VCHORDRQ session configuration failed " 

691 f"after pool reset — connection will be terminated: {e}" 

692 ) 

693 raise 

694 

695 async def _create_pool_once() -> None: 

696 # STEP 1: Bootstrap - ensure vector extension exists BEFORE pool creation. 

697 # On a fresh database, register_vector() in _init_connection will fail 

698 # if the vector extension doesn't exist yet, because the 'vector' type 

699 # won't be found in pg_catalog. We must create the extension first 

700 # using a standalone bootstrap connection. 

701 # Skip this step if vector support is not enabled. 

702 if self.enable_vector: 

703 bootstrap_conn = await asyncpg.connect( 

704 user=self.user, 

705 password=self.password, 

706 database=self.database, 

707 host=self.host, 

708 port=self.port, 

709 ssl=connection_params.get("ssl"), 

710 ) 

711 try: 

712 await self.configure_vector_extension(bootstrap_conn) 

713 finally: 

714 await bootstrap_conn.close() 

715 

716 # STEP 2: Now safe to create pool with register_vector callback. 

717 # The vector extension is guaranteed to exist at this point (if enabled). 

718 pool = await asyncpg.create_pool( 

719 **connection_params, 

720 init=_init_connection, # register pgvector codec on new connections 

721 reset=_reset_connection, # re-apply VCHORDRQ GUCs after RESET ALL 

722 ) # type: ignore 

723 self.pool = pool 

724 

725 try: 

726 async for attempt in AsyncRetrying( 

727 stop=stop_after_attempt(self.connection_retry_attempts), 

728 retry=retry_if_exception_type(self._transient_exceptions), 

729 wait=wait_strategy, 

730 before_sleep=self._before_sleep, 

731 reraise=True, 

732 ): 

733 with attempt: 

734 await _create_pool_once() 

735 

736 ssl_status = "with SSL" if connection_params.get("ssl") else "without SSL" 

737 logger.info( 

738 f"PostgreSQL, Connected to database at {self.host}:{self.port}/{self.database} {ssl_status}" 

739 ) 

740 except Exception as e: 

741 logger.error( 

742 f"PostgreSQL, Failed to connect database at {self.host}:{self.port}/{self.database}, Got:{e}" 

743 ) 

744 raise 

745 

746 async def _ensure_pool(self) -> None: 

747 """Ensure the connection pool is initialised.""" 

748 if self.pool is None: 

749 async with self._pool_reconnect_lock: 

750 if self.pool is None: 

751 await self.initdb() 

752 

753 async def _reset_pool(self) -> None: 

754 async with self._pool_reconnect_lock: 

755 if self.pool is not None: 755 ↛ 769line 755 didn't jump to line 769 because the condition on line 755 was always true

756 try: 

757 await asyncio.wait_for( 

758 self.pool.close(), timeout=self.pool_close_timeout 

759 ) 

760 except asyncio.TimeoutError: 

761 logger.error( 

762 "PostgreSQL, Timed out closing connection pool after %.2fs", 

763 self.pool_close_timeout, 

764 ) 

765 except Exception as close_error: # pragma: no cover - defensive logging 

766 logger.warning( 

767 f"PostgreSQL, Failed to close existing connection pool cleanly: {close_error!r}" 

768 ) 

769 self.pool = None 

770 

771 async def _before_sleep(self, retry_state: RetryCallState) -> None: 

772 """Hook invoked by tenacity before sleeping between retries.""" 

773 exc = retry_state.outcome.exception() if retry_state.outcome else None 

774 logger.warning( 

775 "PostgreSQL transient connection issue on attempt %s/%s: %r", 

776 retry_state.attempt_number, 

777 self.connection_retry_attempts, 

778 exc, 

779 ) 

780 await self._reset_pool() 

781 

782 async def _run_with_retry( 

783 self, 

784 operation: Callable[[asyncpg.Connection], Awaitable[T]], 

785 *, 

786 with_age: bool = False, 

787 graph_name: str | None = None, 

788 timing_label: str | None = None, 

789 ) -> T: 

790 """ 

791 Execute a database operation with automatic retry for transient failures. 

792 

793 Args: 

794 operation: Async callable that receives an active connection. 

795 with_age: Whether to configure Apache AGE on the connection. 

796 graph_name: AGE graph name; required when with_age is True. 

797 

798 Returns: 

799 The result returned by the operation. 

800 

801 Raises: 

802 Exception: Propagates the last error if all retry attempts fail or a non-transient error occurs. 

803 """ 

804 wait_strategy = ( 

805 wait_exponential( 

806 multiplier=self.connection_retry_backoff, 

807 min=self.connection_retry_backoff, 

808 max=self.connection_retry_backoff_max, 

809 ) 

810 if self.connection_retry_backoff > 0 

811 else wait_fixed(0) 

812 ) 

813 

814 async for attempt in AsyncRetrying( 

815 stop=stop_after_attempt(self.connection_retry_attempts), 

816 retry=retry_if_exception_type(self._transient_exceptions), 

817 wait=wait_strategy, 

818 before_sleep=self._before_sleep, 

819 reraise=True, 

820 ): 

821 with attempt: 

822 await self._ensure_pool() 

823 assert self.pool is not None 

824 if timing_label: 824 ↛ 825line 824 didn't jump to line 825 because the condition on line 824 was never true

825 pool_snapshot_before = self._get_pool_snapshot() 

826 performance_timing_log( 

827 "[%s] pool.acquire waiting %s", 

828 timing_label, 

829 pool_snapshot_before, 

830 ) 

831 acquire_start = time.perf_counter() 

832 async with self.pool.acquire() as connection: # type: ignore[arg-type] 

833 acquire_elapsed = time.perf_counter() - acquire_start 

834 if timing_label: 834 ↛ 835line 834 didn't jump to line 835 because the condition on line 834 was never true

835 pool_snapshot_after = self._get_pool_snapshot() 

836 performance_timing_log( 

837 "[%s] pool.acquire completed in %.4fs %s", 

838 timing_label, 

839 acquire_elapsed, 

840 pool_snapshot_after, 

841 ) 

842 if with_age and graph_name: 

843 await self.configure_age(connection, graph_name) 

844 elif with_age and not graph_name: 844 ↛ 845line 844 didn't jump to line 845 because the condition on line 844 was never true

845 raise ValueError("Graph name is required when with_age is True") 

846 return await operation(connection) 

847 

848 def _get_pool_snapshot(self) -> str: 

849 """Best-effort snapshot of asyncpg pool state for diagnostics. 

850 

851 Uses asyncpg private attributes defensively; if a field is unavailable in the 

852 installed asyncpg version, return '?' for that metric instead of failing. 

853 """ 

854 pool = self.pool 

855 if pool is None: 

856 return "pool_state=uninitialized" 

857 

858 holders = getattr(pool, "_holders", None) 

859 queue = getattr(pool, "_queue", None) 

860 max_size = getattr(pool, "_maxsize", None) 

861 min_size = getattr(pool, "_minsize", None) 

862 

863 total_holders = len(holders) if holders is not None else "?" 

864 idle_count: int | str = "?" 

865 acquired_count: int | str = "?" 

866 

867 if holders is not None: 

868 idle_count = 0 

869 acquired_count = 0 

870 for holder in holders: 

871 # asyncpg holder uses _in_use Future/Event-like marker; treat present value as acquired 

872 in_use_marker = getattr(holder, "_in_use", None) 

873 if in_use_marker: 

874 acquired_count += 1 

875 else: 

876 idle_count += 1 

877 

878 waiting_count: int | str = "?" 

879 if queue is not None: 

880 getters = getattr(queue, "_getters", None) 

881 if getters is not None: 

882 waiting_count = len(getters) 

883 

884 return ( 

885 f"pool_state[min={min_size}, max={max_size}, holders={total_holders}, " 

886 f"acquired={acquired_count}, idle={idle_count}, waiting={waiting_count}]" 

887 ) 

888 

889 async def configure_vector_extension(self, connection: asyncpg.Connection) -> None: 

890 """Create VECTOR extension if it doesn't exist for vector similarity operations. 

891 

892 When vector_index_type is HNSW_HALFVEC, validates that pgvector >= 0.7.0 

893 (required for halfvec support) and raises RuntimeError if older. 

894 """ 

895 try: 

896 await connection.execute("CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector") # type: ignore 

897 logger.info("PostgreSQL, VECTOR extension enabled") 

898 except Exception as e: 

899 logger.warning(f"Could not create VECTOR extension: {e}") 

900 # Don't raise - let the system continue without vector extension 

901 return 

902 

903 if getattr(self, "vector_index_type", None) == "HNSW_HALFVEC": 

904 row = await connection.fetchrow( 

905 "SELECT extversion FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'vector'" 

906 ) 

907 if not row or not row["extversion"]: 

908 raise RuntimeError( 

909 "POSTGRES_VECTOR_INDEX_TYPE=HNSW_HALFVEC requires the pgvector " 

910 "extension. Ensure it is installed and CREATE EXTENSION vector succeeded." 

911 ) 

912 raw_version = row["extversion"] 

913 try: 

914 parts = [int(p) for p in str(raw_version).split(".")[:3]] 

915 while len(parts) < 3: 

916 parts.append(0) 

917 version_tuple = (parts[0], parts[1], parts[2]) 

918 except (ValueError, IndexError): 

919 raise RuntimeError( 

920 f"Could not parse pgvector version {raw_version!r}. " 

921 "HNSW_HALFVEC requires pgvector >= 0.7.0." 

922 ) from None 

923 if version_tuple < (0, 7, 0): 

924 raise RuntimeError( 

925 f"POSTGRES_VECTOR_INDEX_TYPE=HNSW_HALFVEC requires pgvector >= 0.7.0, " 

926 f"but installed version is {raw_version}. Upgrade the pgvector extension " 

927 "or use a different index type (e.g. HNSW with embeddings <= 2000 dimensions)." 

928 ) 

929 

930 @staticmethod 

931 async def configure_age_extension(connection: asyncpg.Connection) -> None: 

932 """Refuse AGE versions known to break PGGraphStorage, then create the extension. 

933 

934 AGE 1.8.0 changed Cypher ``id()`` to return ``graphid``. That breaks 

935 ``get_knowledge_graph`` twice over: the labelled branch fails on the 

936 ``graphid`` -> ``bigint`` column cast, and the wildcard branch segfaults the 

937 backend, taking the whole instance through crash recovery. The wildcard is 

938 what the WebUI issues by default, so this is refused at startup rather than 

939 left to surface as an instance-wide crash on the first graph request. 

940 

941 See https://github.com/apache/age/issues/2500. 

942 """ 

943 # Read before the catalog lookup, so that the override also covers a lookup that 

944 # itself fails; otherwise that one path would be an unbypassable startup failure. 

945 override_set = get_env_value(AGE_ALLOW_UNSUPPORTED_ENV, False, bool) 

946 

947 # Decide before creating. CREATE EXTENSION writes pg_extension.extversion, and 

948 # AGE ships no downgrade script, so creating first would leave every refused 

949 # startup with a version the operator cannot lower again -- see the stale-catalog 

950 # paragraph below for what that state costs them. 

951 installed_raw: Any = None 

952 available_raw: Any = None 

953 version_known = True 

954 # Tracked separately from available_raw for the same reason _parse_age_version has 

955 # a sentinel: "the view said nothing" and "the view could not be read" are 

956 # different states, and collapsing them into None would let a failed lookup pass 

957 # for evidence that AGE is absent. 

958 available_unreadable = False 

959 # Two states set available_unreadable -- the view raised, or it named 'age' with a 

960 # NULL default_version -- and they are the same decision but not the same fact. 

961 # Kept apart so the operator-facing text never reports an error that did not 

962 # happen. Only read when available_unreadable is True. 

963 # 

964 # Deliberately initialised to None rather than to either state's wording: a default 

965 # that reads as one of the two states would let a future third writer set the flag 

966 # without setting these, and the operator would then be told about an error that 

967 # did not happen -- the exact failure this pair exists to prevent. With None, every 

968 # site that sets the flag must supply the value, so the omission cannot pass 

969 # silently. 

970 available_unreadable_reason: str | None = None 

971 available_unreadable_display: str | None = None 

972 

973 try: 

974 installed_raw = await connection.fetchval(AGE_INSTALLED_SQL) 

975 except Exception as e: 

976 if isinstance(e, TRANSIENT_DB_EXCEPTIONS): 

977 # Checked before the override, because a connection blip is not a 

978 # version-determination outcome at all: the server never got to answer. 

979 # The override exists to tolerate an unsupported or undeterminable 

980 # version, not to turn a blip into a silently skipped safety gate -- with 

981 # the opposite order the blip would be swallowed and the retry below 

982 # would never happen. 

983 # 

984 # Propagate it unwrapped so that the _run_with_retry wrapping this call 

985 # can recognise and retry it -- wrapping it in RuntimeError would make a 

986 # transient startup blip a permanent startup failure. 

987 # 

988 # A statement or lock timeout (QueryCanceledError) is not in that tuple, 

989 # so it refuses instead of retrying. Deliberate: the tuple is what 

990 # _run_with_retry uses everywhere else in this file, and this gate is not 

991 # the place to redefine cluster-wide retry policy. The override covers the 

992 # case, and the catalog read is a cheap unlocked lookup, so a timeout there 

993 # means the server is in no state to be answering for the AGE version 

994 # anyway. 

995 raise 

996 if override_set: 

997 # Names the consequence rather than deferring to the generic 

998 # could-not-determine wording: version_known = False skips the available 

999 # lookup entirely, so unlike every other override state the gate ends up 

1000 # having seen nothing at all, and the CREATE EXTENSION below still runs. 

1001 # Says nothing about whether 'age' is registered here -- that is precisely 

1002 # what the failed lookup did not establish. 

1003 logger.warning( 

1004 f"PostgreSQL, could not determine the Apache AGE version ({e}), but " 

1005 f"{AGE_ALLOW_UNSUPPORTED_ENV} is set, so PGGraphStorage is starting " 

1006 "anyway. The available-version lookup is skipped in this state, so " 

1007 "nothing has inspected the Apache AGE that CREATE EXTENSION may be " 

1008 "about to install. If that AGE is 1.8.0 or newer, a single " 

1009 "get_knowledge_graph request may take the whole PostgreSQL instance " 

1010 "through crash recovery." 

1011 ) 

1012 version_known = False 

1013 else: 

1014 raise RuntimeError( 

1015 f"Could not determine the Apache AGE version ({e}). PGGraphStorage " 

1016 "needs it in order to reject versions that crash the PostgreSQL backend " 

1017 "(https://github.com/apache/age/issues/2500). Set " 

1018 f"{AGE_ALLOW_UNSUPPORTED_ENV}=true to start anyway, at your own risk." 

1019 ) from e 

1020 

1021 if version_known: 

1022 try: 

1023 # fetchrow, not fetchval: default_version is NULLABLE, so fetchval returns 

1024 # None both for "no row" and for "a row whose value is NULL". Those are 

1025 # opposite facts -- 'age' absent from the extension path, versus an 

1026 # age.control that is on disk (so age.so may be too) but names no version 

1027 # -- and collapsing them lets a present-but-unversioned AGE read as absent. 

1028 available_row = await connection.fetchrow(AGE_AVAILABLE_SQL) 

1029 except Exception as e: 

1030 if isinstance(e, TRANSIENT_DB_EXCEPTIONS): 

1031 raise 

1032 # Anything else here is the sharedir view failing over a control file that 

1033 # need not be AGE's, which is no evidence about AGE either way -- but it 

1034 # is also no evidence that AGE is absent, and pg_extension cannot stand in 

1035 # for it because extversion does not move when the binaries are swapped. 

1036 # The flag below therefore does two things: it keeps this from being read 

1037 # as "AGE is absent", and it makes the version undeterminable rather than 

1038 # letting pg_extension decide alone. 

1039 logger.warning( 

1040 "PostgreSQL, could not read the available Apache AGE version from " 

1041 f"pg_available_extensions ({e}); the version cannot be confirmed from " 

1042 "pg_extension alone, because it does not track the loaded binaries." 

1043 ) 

1044 available_unreadable = True 

1045 available_unreadable_reason = ( 

1046 "pg_available_extensions could not be read" 

1047 ) 

1048 available_unreadable_display = "<lookup failed>" 

1049 else: 

1050 if available_row is None: 

1051 # No control file for 'age' anywhere on the extension path, so the 

1052 # view genuinely has nothing to say: AGE is absent. 

1053 available_raw = None 

1054 elif available_row["default_version"] is None: 

1055 # age.control is on disk -- so age.so may well be too -- but the file 

1056 # names no version. Present-and-unreadable, not absent: pg_extension 

1057 # must not decide alone, because extversion cannot see a binary swap. 

1058 available_unreadable = True 

1059 available_unreadable_reason = "pg_available_extensions names 'age' but reports no version for it" 

1060 available_unreadable_display = "<no version reported>" 

1061 else: 

1062 available_raw = available_row["default_version"] 

1063 

1064 if installed_raw is None and available_unreadable: 

1065 # Not the nothing-to-gate state below: 'age' is merely absent from 

1066 # pg_extension, and the one source that could have reported an AGE sitting on 

1067 # disk gave no usable answer. Falling through would CREATE EXTENSION -- and 

1068 # register whatever version is there -- without the gate ever having seen it, 

1069 # which is precisely the crash this function exists to prevent. 

1070 if not override_set: 

1071 # Refusing outright would be wrong too: nothing here is evidence of an 

1072 # unsupported version. So neither create nor refuse; leave the database as 

1073 # it was found. 

1074 logger.warning( 

1075 "PostgreSQL, the Apache AGE version could not be determined because " 

1076 f"{available_unreadable_reason}, and 'age' is not registered " 

1077 "in this database. Skipping CREATE EXTENSION so that the gate does not " 

1078 "install an AGE version it never checked. Set " 

1079 f"{AGE_ALLOW_UNSUPPORTED_ENV}=true to create it anyway, at your own risk." 

1080 ) 

1081 return 

1082 # Named separately from the generic could-not-determine warning below, because 

1083 # the consequence is not the generic one: everywhere else the override starts a 

1084 # deployment against an AGE that is already there, while here CREATE EXTENSION 

1085 # is about to install one that nothing has looked at. 

1086 logger.warning( 

1087 "PostgreSQL, 'age' is not registered in this database and " 

1088 f"{available_unreadable_reason}, so the version of any Apache AGE on disk " 

1089 f"is unknown, but {AGE_ALLOW_UNSUPPORTED_ENV} is set, so CREATE EXTENSION " 

1090 "is installing it without the gate having seen it. If that AGE is 1.8.0 or " 

1091 "newer, a single get_knowledge_graph request may take the whole PostgreSQL " 

1092 "instance through crash recovery." 

1093 ) 

1094 # This warning has already named the consequence for this state, so suppress 

1095 # the generic one: the branches below are all guarded on version_known. 

1096 version_known = False 

1097 

1098 if ( 

1099 version_known 

1100 and installed_raw is None 

1101 and available_raw is None 

1102 and not available_unreadable 

1103 ): 

1104 # Neither catalog names 'age': the extension is not on disk and not registered 

1105 # in this database, so no ag_catalog functions exist to call, no age.so gets 

1106 # loaded, and there is nothing to gate. 

1107 # Logged at INFO, not DEBUG: this is the one state in which the gate proceeds 

1108 # without having checked anything, so it must be visible at the default level. 

1109 logger.info( 

1110 "PostgreSQL, no Apache AGE version check was performed: neither " 

1111 "pg_available_extensions nor pg_extension names 'age', so AGE is not " 

1112 "installed on this server and there is nothing to gate" 

1113 ) 

1114 elif version_known: 

1115 # Rendered distinctly from `available=None`: an operator reading this needs to 

1116 # see that no version came back, not that the view answered "absent" -- and 

1117 # which of the two it was, since a lookup that raised and a control file that 

1118 # names no version call for different things to go and look at. 

1119 available_found = ( 

1120 available_unreadable_display 

1121 if available_unreadable 

1122 else repr(available_raw) 

1123 ) 

1124 found = f"installed={installed_raw!r} available={available_found}" 

1125 installed_parsed = _parse_age_version(installed_raw) 

1126 # A source that gave no usable answer -- the lookup raised, or the row named no 

1127 # version -- is not a source that said nothing, so it gets the same sentinel as 

1128 # a value we could not parse. pg_available_extensions is 

1129 # the source that tracks the binaries; pg_extension.extversion cannot see a 

1130 # binary swap, so letting it decide alone here would start a deployment whose 

1131 # loaded age.so was never checked. Fail closed instead -- the override still 

1132 # covers this state, as it does every other refusal. 

1133 available_parsed = ( 

1134 _AGE_VERSION_UNPARSEABLE 

1135 if available_unreadable 

1136 else _parse_age_version(available_raw) 

1137 ) 

1138 candidates = (installed_parsed, available_parsed) 

1139 parsed = [c for c in candidates if isinstance(c, tuple)] 

1140 

1141 # The higher of the two decides: a stale catalog must not mask newer binaries. 

1142 # An unreadable sibling source cannot make the situation safer, so a version we 

1143 # can read and know to be unsupported is reported as such before anything else. 

1144 if parsed and max(parsed) >= AGE_FIRST_UNSUPPORTED_VERSION: 

1145 raw_version = ".".join(str(p) for p in max(parsed)) 

1146 unsupported = ".".join(str(p) for p in AGE_FIRST_UNSUPPORTED_VERSION) 

1147 if override_set: 

1148 logger.warning( 

1149 f"PostgreSQL, Apache AGE {raw_version} ({found}) is known to break " 

1150 f"PGGraphStorage's graph queries, but {AGE_ALLOW_UNSUPPORTED_ENV} is set, " 

1151 "so the check is being skipped. A single graph request may take the whole " 

1152 "PostgreSQL instance through crash recovery." 

1153 ) 

1154 else: 

1155 message = ( 

1156 f"Apache AGE {raw_version} is not supported by PGGraphStorage ({found}): from " 

1157 f"{unsupported} onward, get_knowledge_graph fails, and a graph query can terminate " 

1158 "the PostgreSQL backend with SIGSEGV and take the whole instance through crash " 

1159 "recovery (https://github.com/apache/age/issues/2500). Verified good: AGE 1.7.0. " 

1160 ) 

1161 if ( 

1162 isinstance(installed_parsed, tuple) 

1163 and installed_parsed >= AGE_FIRST_UNSUPPORTED_VERSION 

1164 and isinstance(available_parsed, tuple) 

1165 and available_parsed < AGE_FIRST_UNSUPPORTED_VERSION 

1166 ): 

1167 # The generic remedies are assembled only in the other cells, 

1168 # because neither one applies here: pinning is what produced this 

1169 # state, and the override would start a deployment whose graph 

1170 # reads all fail. Offering them and then withdrawing them, as the 

1171 # text used to, reads as a contradiction to the operator. 

1172 message += ( 

1173 "Here pg_extension records the newer AGE script while age.control " 

1174 "reports the older one, so the older library is what loads: AGE is " 

1175 "then non-functional rather than crash-prone. Writes still go through " 

1176 "-- CREATE ... RETURN n succeeds -- but every MATCH fails with 'ag " 

1177 "function does not exist' because the newer script declares functions " 

1178 "the older library does not export, so nothing can be read back. " 

1179 "ALTER EXTENSION age UPDATE cannot repair this -- AGE ships no " 

1180 "downgrade script, so extversion cannot be lowered, and " 

1181 f"{AGE_ALLOW_UNSUPPORTED_ENV}=true only starts a deployment in that " 

1182 "same read-broken state. The ways out are to restore the newer " 

1183 "binaries, which PGGraphStorage will then refuse as unsupported, to " 

1184 "DROP EXTENSION age CASCADE and recreate the graph, or to switch " 

1185 "LIGHTRAG_GRAPH_STORAGE to PGTableGraphStorage, which needs no " 

1186 "PostgreSQL extension." 

1187 ) 

1188 else: 

1189 message += ( 

1190 "Pin AGE to a verified version, or switch LIGHTRAG_GRAPH_STORAGE to " 

1191 "PGTableGraphStorage, which needs no PostgreSQL extension. If installed and " 

1192 "available differ above, the binaries were swapped under an existing data " 

1193 "directory without ALTER EXTENSION age UPDATE; the loaded binaries are what runs. " 

1194 "AGE also reports its version per release rather than per commit, so a build that " 

1195 f"fixes the crash may still report {raw_version}; set " 

1196 f"{AGE_ALLOW_UNSUPPORTED_ENV}=true to run against such a build at your own risk." 

1197 ) 

1198 raise RuntimeError(message) 

1199 

1200 # Either nothing parsed, or one source is present but unreadable. An unverified 

1201 # version is not a safe one, so fail closed even when the sibling looks fine. 

1202 elif any(c is _AGE_VERSION_UNPARSEABLE for c in candidates) or not parsed: 

1203 if override_set: 

1204 logger.warning( 

1205 f"PostgreSQL, could not determine the Apache AGE version ({found}), " 

1206 f"but {AGE_ALLOW_UNSUPPORTED_ENV} is set, so PGGraphStorage is " 

1207 "starting anyway." 

1208 ) 

1209 else: 

1210 raise RuntimeError( 

1211 f"Could not determine the Apache AGE version ({found}). PGGraphStorage " 

1212 "needs it in order to reject versions that crash the PostgreSQL backend " 

1213 "(https://github.com/apache/age/issues/2500). Set " 

1214 f"{AGE_ALLOW_UNSUPPORTED_ENV}=true to start anyway, at your own risk." 

1215 ) 

1216 

1217 try: 

1218 await connection.execute("CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS AGE CASCADE") # type: ignore 

1219 logger.info("PostgreSQL, AGE extension enabled") 

1220 except Exception as e: 

1221 # Non-fatal, as before: the system may run without AGE. On a server that has 

1222 # never had it this is where the pre-existing 'extension "age" is not 

1223 # available' lands, which is why the no-AGE path above falls through to here 

1224 # rather than returning. 

1225 logger.warning(f"Could not create AGE extension: {e}") 

1226 

1227 async def configure_age( 

1228 self, connection: asyncpg.Connection, graph_name: str 

1229 ) -> None: 

1230 """Prepare a pooled connection for Apache AGE access. 

1231 

1232 Two very different things are needed before an AGE statement can run, 

1233 and they have very different lifetimes: 

1234 

1235 - ``SET search_path`` is genuine session state. ``_reset_connection`` 

1236 deliberately runs ``RESET ALL`` on every pool release so an AGE 

1237 search_path never leaks into a non-AGE checkout, which means it has 

1238 to be re-applied on every checkout. 

1239 - The graph itself is one-time DDL. Creating it here unconditionally 

1240 made PostgreSQL log an ERROR/STATEMENT pair for *every* graph read 

1241 and write, because the server writes its log entry before the client 

1242 ever sees the error and can swallow it. Graph 

1243 existence is now handled by :meth:`_ensure_age_graph`, which reaches 

1244 the database at most once per process. 

1245 """ 

1246 await connection.execute( # type: ignore 

1247 'SET search_path = ag_catalog, "$user", public' 

1248 ) 

1249 await self._ensure_age_graph(connection, graph_name) 

1250 

1251 async def _ensure_age_graph( 

1252 self, connection: asyncpg.Connection, graph_name: str 

1253 ) -> None: 

1254 """Create the AGE graph if it does not exist, at most once per process. 

1255 

1256 Steady state is a set membership test and no SQL at all. On a miss the 

1257 graph is looked up in ``ag_catalog.ag_graph`` and ``create_graph()`` is 

1258 only issued when it is genuinely absent, so a running server stops 

1259 producing "graph already exists" errors entirely. 

1260 

1261 Apache AGE takes no lock before its own existence check (see 

1262 ``create_graph_internal`` upstream), so concurrent first-time creation 

1263 can still race past the lookup. Both known outcomes are tolerated: 

1264 

1265 - ``InvalidSchemaNameError`` (3F000) — AGE reports "graph already 

1266 exists" with ``ERRCODE_UNDEFINED_SCHEMA``. 

1267 - ``UniqueViolationError`` (23505) — the loser of the ``ag_graph`` 

1268 name index race. 

1269 

1270 The graph is recorded as ensured only once it is known to exist. A 

1271 transient failure must leave the cache untouched, otherwise a graph 

1272 that was never created would be assumed present for the lifetime of 

1273 the process and every later operation would fail with 3F000. 

1274 """ 

1275 if graph_name in self._ensured_age_graphs: 

1276 return 

1277 

1278 async with self._age_graph_ensure_lock: 

1279 # A concurrent task may have ensured the graph while we waited. 

1280 if graph_name in self._ensured_age_graphs: 1280 ↛ 1281line 1280 didn't jump to line 1281 because the condition on line 1280 was never true

1281 return 

1282 

1283 # The parameter has to be truncated the same way the stored value 

1284 # was. PostgreSQL's `name` type holds 63 bytes, and create_graph() 

1285 # below passes the name as a literal, which PostgreSQL silently 

1286 # clips -- so a workspace long enough to overflow is stored clipped 

1287 # and would never match an untruncated comparison. Casting the 

1288 # bind parameter straight to `name` is not an option: for a 

1289 # parameter (unlike a literal) PostgreSQL raises 42622 

1290 # "identifier too long" instead of clipping. left() is safe 

1291 # because _get_workspace_graph_name() reduces the name to 

1292 # [A-Za-z0-9_], where one character is one byte. 

1293 exists = await connection.fetchval( # type: ignore 

1294 "SELECT 1 FROM ag_catalog.ag_graph " 

1295 f"WHERE name = left($1, {_PG_NAME_MAX_BYTES})::name", 

1296 graph_name, 

1297 ) 

1298 if exists is None: 

1299 try: 

1300 await connection.execute( # type: ignore 

1301 f"select create_graph('{graph_name}')" 

1302 ) 

1303 logger.info(f"PostgreSQL, AGE graph created: {graph_name}") 

1304 except ( 

1305 asyncpg.exceptions.InvalidSchemaNameError, 

1306 asyncpg.exceptions.UniqueViolationError, 

1307 ) as e: 

1308 # Lost the creation race: the graph exists now, which is 

1309 # all this method promises. 

1310 logger.debug( 

1311 "PostgreSQL, AGE graph %s concurrently created elsewhere: %r", 

1312 graph_name, 

1313 e, 

1314 ) 

1315 

1316 self._ensured_age_graphs.add(graph_name) 

1317 

1318 async def configure_vchordrq(self, connection: asyncpg.Connection) -> None: 

1319 """Configure VCHORDRQ extension for vector similarity search. 

1320 

1321 Raises: 

1322 asyncpg.exceptions.UndefinedObjectError: If VCHORDRQ extension is not installed 

1323 asyncpg.exceptions.InvalidParameterValueError: If parameter value is invalid 

1324 

1325 Note: 

1326 This method does not catch exceptions. Configuration errors will fail-fast, 

1327 while transient connection errors will be retried by _run_with_retry. 

1328 """ 

1329 # Handle probes parameter - only set if non-empty value is provided 

1330 if self.vchordrq_probes and str(self.vchordrq_probes).strip(): 

1331 await connection.execute(f"SET vchordrq.probes TO '{self.vchordrq_probes}'") 

1332 logger.debug(f"PostgreSQL, VCHORDRQ probes set to: {self.vchordrq_probes}") 

1333 

1334 # Handle epsilon parameter independently - check for None to allow 0.0 as valid value 

1335 if self.vchordrq_epsilon is not None: 

1336 await connection.execute(f"SET vchordrq.epsilon TO {self.vchordrq_epsilon}") 

1337 logger.debug( 

1338 f"PostgreSQL, VCHORDRQ epsilon set to: {self.vchordrq_epsilon}" 

1339 ) 

1340 

1341 async def _migrate_llm_cache_schema(self): 

1342 """Migrate LLM cache schema: add new columns and remove deprecated mode field""" 

1343 try: 

1344 # Check if all columns exist 

1345 check_columns_sql = """ 

1346 SELECT column_name 

1347 FROM information_schema.columns 

1348 WHERE table_name = 'lightrag_llm_cache' 

1349 AND column_name IN ('chunk_id', 'cache_type', 'queryparam', 'mode') 

1350 """ 

1351 

1352 existing_columns = await self.query(check_columns_sql, multirows=True) 

1353 existing_column_names = ( 

1354 {col["column_name"] for col in existing_columns} 

1355 if existing_columns 

1356 else set() 

1357 ) 

1358 

1359 # Add missing chunk_id column 

1360 if "chunk_id" not in existing_column_names: 

1361 logger.info("Adding chunk_id column to LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE table") 

1362 add_chunk_id_sql = """ 

1363 ALTER TABLE LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE 

1364 ADD COLUMN chunk_id VARCHAR(255) NULL 

1365 """ 

1366 await self.execute(add_chunk_id_sql) 

1367 logger.info( 

1368 "Successfully added chunk_id column to LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE table" 

1369 ) 

1370 else: 

1371 logger.info( 

1372 "chunk_id column already exists in LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE table" 

1373 ) 

1374 

1375 # Add missing cache_type column 

1376 if "cache_type" not in existing_column_names: 

1377 logger.info("Adding cache_type column to LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE table") 

1378 add_cache_type_sql = """ 

1379 ALTER TABLE LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE 

1380 ADD COLUMN cache_type VARCHAR(32) NULL 

1381 """ 

1382 await self.execute(add_cache_type_sql) 

1383 logger.info( 

1384 "Successfully added cache_type column to LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE table" 

1385 ) 

1386 

1387 # Migrate existing data using optimized regex pattern 

1388 logger.info( 

1389 "Migrating existing LLM cache data to populate cache_type field (optimized)" 

1390 ) 

1391 optimized_update_sql = """ 

1392 UPDATE LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE 

1393 SET cache_type = CASE 

1394 WHEN id ~ '^[^:]+:[^:]+:' THEN split_part(id, ':', 2) 

1395 ELSE 'extract' 

1396 END 

1397 WHERE cache_type IS NULL 

1398 """ 

1399 await self.execute(optimized_update_sql) 

1400 logger.info("Successfully migrated existing LLM cache data") 

1401 else: 

1402 logger.info( 

1403 "cache_type column already exists in LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE table" 

1404 ) 

1405 

1406 # Add missing queryparam column 

1407 if "queryparam" not in existing_column_names: 

1408 logger.info("Adding queryparam column to LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE table") 

1409 add_queryparam_sql = """ 

1410 ALTER TABLE LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE 

1411 ADD COLUMN queryparam JSONB NULL 

1412 """ 

1413 await self.execute(add_queryparam_sql) 

1414 logger.info( 

1415 "Successfully added queryparam column to LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE table" 

1416 ) 

1417 else: 

1418 logger.info( 

1419 "queryparam column already exists in LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE table" 

1420 ) 

1421 

1422 # Remove deprecated mode field if it exists 

1423 if "mode" in existing_column_names: 

1424 logger.info( 

1425 "Removing deprecated mode column from LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE table" 

1426 ) 

1427 

1428 # First, drop the primary key constraint that includes mode 

1429 drop_pk_sql = """ 

1430 ALTER TABLE LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE 

1431 DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE_PK 

1432 """ 

1433 await self.execute(drop_pk_sql) 

1434 logger.info("Dropped old primary key constraint") 

1435 

1436 # Drop the mode column 

1437 drop_mode_sql = """ 

1438 ALTER TABLE LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE 

1439 DROP COLUMN mode 

1440 """ 

1441 await self.execute(drop_mode_sql) 

1442 logger.info( 

1443 "Successfully removed mode column from LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE table" 

1444 ) 

1445 

1446 # Create new primary key constraint without mode 

1447 add_pk_sql = """ 

1448 ALTER TABLE LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE 

1449 ADD CONSTRAINT LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE_PK PRIMARY KEY (workspace, id) 

1450 """ 

1451 await self.execute(add_pk_sql) 

1452 logger.info("Created new primary key constraint (workspace, id)") 

1453 else: 

1454 logger.info("mode column does not exist in LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE table") 

1455 

1456 except Exception as e: 

1457 logger.warning(f"Failed to migrate LLM cache schema: {e}") 

1458 

1459 async def _migrate_timestamp_columns(self): 

1460 """Migrate timestamp columns in tables to witimezone-free types, assuming original data is in UTC time""" 

1461 # Tables and columns that need migration 

1462 tables_to_migrate = { 

1463 "LIGHTRAG_VDB_ENTITY": ["create_time", "update_time"], 

1464 "LIGHTRAG_VDB_RELATION": ["create_time", "update_time"], 

1465 "LIGHTRAG_DOC_CHUNKS": ["create_time", "update_time"], 

1466 "LIGHTRAG_DOC_STATUS": ["created_at", "updated_at"], 

1467 } 

1468 

1469 try: 

1470 # Filter out tables that don't exist (e.g., legacy vector tables may not exist) 

1471 existing_tables = {} 

1472 for table_name, columns in tables_to_migrate.items(): 

1473 if await self.check_table_exists(table_name): 

1474 existing_tables[table_name] = columns 

1475 else: 

1476 logger.debug( 

1477 f"Table {table_name} does not exist, skipping timestamp migration" 

1478 ) 

1479 

1480 # Skip if no tables to migrate 

1481 if not existing_tables: 

1482 logger.debug("No tables found for timestamp migration") 

1483 return 

1484 

1485 # Use filtered tables for migration 

1486 tables_to_migrate = existing_tables 

1487 

1488 # Optimization: Batch check all columns in one query instead of 8 separate queries 

1489 table_names_lower = [t.lower() for t in tables_to_migrate.keys()] 

1490 all_column_names = list( 

1491 set(col for cols in tables_to_migrate.values() for col in cols) 

1492 ) 

1493 

1494 check_all_columns_sql = """ 

1495 SELECT table_name, column_name, data_type 

1496 FROM information_schema.columns 

1497 WHERE table_name = ANY($1) 

1498 AND column_name = ANY($2) 

1499 """ 

1500 

1501 all_columns_result = await self.query( 

1502 check_all_columns_sql, 

1503 [table_names_lower, all_column_names], 

1504 multirows=True, 

1505 ) 

1506 

1507 # Build lookup dict: (table_name, column_name) -> data_type 

1508 column_types = {} 

1509 if all_columns_result: 

1510 column_types = { 

1511 (row["table_name"].upper(), row["column_name"]): row["data_type"] 

1512 for row in all_columns_result 

1513 } 

1514 

1515 # Now iterate and migrate only what's needed 

1516 for table_name, columns in tables_to_migrate.items(): 

1517 for column_name in columns: 

1518 try: 

1519 data_type = column_types.get((table_name, column_name)) 

1520 

1521 if not data_type: 

1522 logger.warning( 

1523 f"Column {table_name}.{column_name} does not exist, skipping migration" 

1524 ) 

1525 continue 

1526 

1527 # Check column type 

1528 if data_type == "timestamp without time zone": 

1529 logger.debug( 

1530 f"Column {table_name}.{column_name} is already witimezone-free, no migration needed" 

1531 ) 

1532 continue 

1533 

1534 # Execute migration, explicitly specifying UTC timezone for interpreting original data 

1535 logger.info( 

1536 f"Migrating {table_name}.{column_name} from {data_type} to TIMESTAMP(0) type" 

1537 ) 

1538 migration_sql = f""" 

1539 ALTER TABLE {table_name} 

1540 ALTER COLUMN {column_name} TYPE TIMESTAMP(0), 

1541 ALTER COLUMN {column_name} SET DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP 

1542 """ 

1543 

1544 await self.execute(migration_sql) 

1545 logger.info( 

1546 f"Successfully migrated {table_name}.{column_name} to timezone-free type" 

1547 ) 

1548 except Exception as e: 

1549 # Log error but don't interrupt the process 

1550 logger.warning( 

1551 f"Failed to migrate {table_name}.{column_name}: {e}" 

1552 ) 

1553 except Exception as e: 

1554 logger.error(f"Failed to batch check timestamp columns: {e}") 

1555 

1556 async def _migrate_doc_chunks_to_vdb_chunks(self): 

1557 """ 

1558 Migrate data from LIGHTRAG_DOC_CHUNKS to LIGHTRAG_VDB_CHUNKS if specific conditions are met. 

1559 This migration is intended for users who are upgrading and have an older table structure 

1560 where LIGHTRAG_DOC_CHUNKS contained a `content_vector` column. 

1561 

1562 """ 

1563 try: 

1564 # 0. Check if both tables exist before proceeding 

1565 vdb_chunks_exists = await self.check_table_exists("LIGHTRAG_VDB_CHUNKS") 

1566 doc_chunks_exists = await self.check_table_exists("LIGHTRAG_DOC_CHUNKS") 

1567 

1568 if not vdb_chunks_exists: 

1569 logger.debug( 

1570 "Skipping migration: LIGHTRAG_VDB_CHUNKS table does not exist" 

1571 ) 

1572 return 

1573 

1574 if not doc_chunks_exists: 

1575 logger.debug( 

1576 "Skipping migration: LIGHTRAG_DOC_CHUNKS table does not exist" 

1577 ) 

1578 return 

1579 

1580 # 1. Check if the new table LIGHTRAG_VDB_CHUNKS is empty 

1581 vdb_chunks_count_sql = "SELECT COUNT(1) as count FROM LIGHTRAG_VDB_CHUNKS" 

1582 vdb_chunks_count_result = await self.query(vdb_chunks_count_sql) 

1583 if vdb_chunks_count_result and vdb_chunks_count_result["count"] > 0: 

1584 logger.info( 

1585 "Skipping migration: LIGHTRAG_VDB_CHUNKS already contains data." 

1586 ) 

1587 return 

1588 

1589 # 2. Check if `content_vector` column exists in the old table 

1590 check_column_sql = """ 

1591 SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns 

1592 WHERE table_name = 'lightrag_doc_chunks' AND column_name = 'content_vector' 

1593 """ 

1594 column_exists = await self.query(check_column_sql) 

1595 if not column_exists: 

1596 logger.info( 

1597 "Skipping migration: `content_vector` not found in LIGHTRAG_DOC_CHUNKS" 

1598 ) 

1599 return 

1600 

1601 # 3. Check if the old table LIGHTRAG_DOC_CHUNKS has data 

1602 doc_chunks_count_sql = "SELECT COUNT(1) as count FROM LIGHTRAG_DOC_CHUNKS" 

1603 doc_chunks_count_result = await self.query(doc_chunks_count_sql) 

1604 if not doc_chunks_count_result or doc_chunks_count_result["count"] == 0: 

1605 logger.info("Skipping migration: LIGHTRAG_DOC_CHUNKS is empty.") 

1606 return 

1607 

1608 # 4. Perform the migration 

1609 logger.info( 

1610 "Starting data migration from LIGHTRAG_DOC_CHUNKS to LIGHTRAG_VDB_CHUNKS..." 

1611 ) 

1612 migration_sql = """ 

1613 INSERT INTO LIGHTRAG_VDB_CHUNKS ( 

1614 id, workspace, full_doc_id, chunk_order_index, tokens, content, 

1615 content_vector, file_path, create_time, update_time 

1616 ) 

1617 SELECT 

1618 id, workspace, full_doc_id, chunk_order_index, tokens, content, 

1619 content_vector, file_path, create_time, update_time 

1620 FROM LIGHTRAG_DOC_CHUNKS 

1621 ON CONFLICT (workspace, id) DO NOTHING; 

1622 """ 

1623 await self.execute(migration_sql) 

1624 logger.info("Data migration to LIGHTRAG_VDB_CHUNKS completed successfully.") 

1625 

1626 except Exception as e: 

1627 logger.error(f"Failed during data migration to LIGHTRAG_VDB_CHUNKS: {e}") 

1628 # Do not re-raise, to allow the application to start 

1629 

1630 async def _check_llm_cache_needs_migration(self): 

1631 """Check if LLM cache data needs migration by examining any record with old format""" 

1632 try: 

1633 # Optimized query: directly check for old format records without sorting 

1634 check_sql = """ 

1635 SELECT 1 FROM LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE 

1636 WHERE id NOT LIKE '%:%' 

1637 LIMIT 1 

1638 """ 

1639 result = await self.query(check_sql) 

1640 

1641 # If any old format record exists, migration is needed 

1642 return result is not None 

1643 

1644 except Exception as e: 

1645 logger.warning(f"Failed to check LLM cache migration status: {e}") 

1646 return False 

1647 

1648 async def _migrate_llm_cache_to_flattened_keys(self): 

1649 """Optimized version: directly execute single UPDATE migration to migrate old format cache keys to flattened format""" 

1650 try: 

1651 # Check if migration is needed 

1652 check_sql = """ 

1653 SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE 

1654 WHERE id NOT LIKE '%:%' 

1655 """ 

1656 result = await self.query(check_sql) 

1657 

1658 if not result or result["count"] == 0: 

1659 logger.info("No old format LLM cache data found, skipping migration") 

1660 return 

1661 

1662 old_count = result["count"] 

1663 logger.info(f"Found {old_count} old format cache records") 

1664 

1665 # Check potential primary key conflicts (optional but recommended) 

1666 conflict_check_sql = """ 

1667 WITH new_ids AS ( 

1668 SELECT 

1669 workspace, 

1670 mode, 

1671 id as old_id, 

1672 mode || ':' || 

1673 CASE WHEN mode = 'default' THEN 'extract' ELSE 'unknown' END || ':' || 

1674 md5(original_prompt) as new_id 

1675 FROM LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE 

1676 WHERE id NOT LIKE '%:%' 

1677 ) 

1678 SELECT COUNT(*) as conflicts 

1679 FROM new_ids n1 

1680 JOIN LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE existing 

1681 ON existing.workspace = n1.workspace 

1682 AND existing.mode = n1.mode 

1683 AND existing.id = n1.new_id 

1684 WHERE existing.id LIKE '%:%' -- Only check conflicts with existing new format records 

1685 """ 

1686 

1687 conflict_result = await self.query(conflict_check_sql) 

1688 if conflict_result and conflict_result["conflicts"] > 0: 

1689 logger.warning( 

1690 f"Found {conflict_result['conflicts']} potential ID conflicts with existing records" 

1691 ) 

1692 # Can choose to continue or abort, here we choose to continue and log warning 

1693 

1694 # Execute single UPDATE migration 

1695 logger.info("Starting optimized LLM cache migration...") 

1696 migration_sql = """ 

1697 UPDATE LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE 

1698 SET 

1699 id = mode || ':' || 

1700 CASE WHEN mode = 'default' THEN 'extract' ELSE 'unknown' END || ':' || 

1701 md5(original_prompt), 

1702 cache_type = CASE WHEN mode = 'default' THEN 'extract' ELSE 'unknown' END, 

1703 update_time = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP 

1704 WHERE id NOT LIKE '%:%' 

1705 """ 

1706 

1707 # Execute migration 

1708 await self.execute(migration_sql) 

1709 

1710 # Verify migration results 

1711 verify_sql = """ 

1712 SELECT COUNT(*) as remaining_old FROM LIGHTRAG_LLM_CACHE 

1713 WHERE id NOT LIKE '%:%' 

1714 """ 

1715 verify_result = await self.query(verify_sql) 

1716 remaining = verify_result["remaining_old"] if verify_result else -1 

1717 

1718 if remaining == 0: 

1719 logger.info( 

1720 f"✅ Successfully migrated {old_count} LLM cache records to flattened format" 

1721 ) 

1722 else: 

1723 logger.warning( 

1724 f"⚠️ Migration completed but {remaining} old format records remain" 

1725 ) 

1726 

1727 except Exception as e: 

1728 logger.error(f"Optimized LLM cache migration failed: {e}") 

1729 raise 

1730

2040 async def _migrate_doc_status_add_scheduling_index(self): 

2041 """Create the keyset-sweep index backing the memory-bounding scheduling 

2042 page API (Phase 1). 

2043 

2044 ``NULLS FIRST`` is load-bearing, not decoration. PostgreSQL's default for 

2045 ``ASC`` is NULLS LAST, so an index declared ``(… created_at, id)`` does 

2046 NOT satisfy ``ORDER BY created_at ASC NULLS FIRST, id ASC`` — the planner 

2047 cannot use it for ordering and falls back to a bitmap scan plus a 

2048 top-N sort of every row past the cursor. Measured at 60k rows: the old 

2049 index sorted 7583 rows per page; with this one the same page is an 

2050 ordered index scan touching exactly ``limit`` rows (500), 4.6ms → 0.23ms. 

2051 

2052 Superseded name: the old index is dropped, because 

2053 ``CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`` on the same name would keep the (wrong) 

2054 existing definition forever. A doc_status index is derived state, so 

2055 rebuilding it is inside the documented upgrade envelope. 

2056 

2057 Order matters: create, VERIFY from ``pg_indexes``, and only then retire 

2058 the superseded index. Dropping first and swallowing a failed create left 

2059 the table with NO scheduling index — strictly worse than before the 

2060 upgrade, and silently: the service starts, pages stay correct and 

2061 memory-bounded (the top-N sort keeps only ``limit`` rows), and only the 

2062 I/O degrades to a full scan plus a sort per page. Verification reads the 

2063 catalog rather than inferring success from the absence of an exception. 

2064 

2065 A missing index is NOT fatal — index DDL can fail transiently (lock 

2066 timeout, concurrent DDL, a role without CREATE) and every startup retries 

2067 — but it is reported at WARNING with the consequence and the DDL to run 

2068 by hand, because nothing else about a degraded plan is observable. 

2069 

2070 Guarded and idempotent — retried on every startup until present. 

2071 """ 

2072 index_name = "idx_lightrag_doc_status_ws_status_created_nf_id" 

2073 create_sql = ( 

2074 f"CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS {index_name} " 

2075 "ON LIGHTRAG_DOC_STATUS " 

2076 "(workspace, status, created_at NULLS FIRST, id)" 

2077 ) 

2078 superseded_name = "idx_lightrag_doc_status_ws_status_created_id" 

2079 

2080 try: 

2081 if not await self._doc_status_index_exists(index_name): 

2082 logger.info(f"Creating index {index_name} on LIGHTRAG_DOC_STATUS") 

2083 await self.execute(create_sql) 

2084 except Exception as e: 

2085 logger.error( 

2086 f"Failed to create index {index_name} on LIGHTRAG_DOC_STATUS: {e}" 

2087 ) 

2088 

2089 try: 

2090 created = await self._doc_status_index_exists(index_name) 

2091 except Exception as verify_error: 

2092 logger.error( 

2093 f"Could not verify scheduling index {index_name}: {verify_error}" 

2094 ) 

2095 created = False 

2096 

2097 if not created: 

2098 logger.warning( 

2099 f"Scheduling index {index_name} is MISSING on LIGHTRAG_DOC_STATUS: " 

2100 "every scheduling page falls back to a full scan plus a per-page " 

2101 "sort (O(rows) I/O per page, O(rows²/page_size) per sweep). " 

2102 f"Keeping the superseded index {superseded_name} so paging is no " 

2103 "worse than before this upgrade; startup retries the creation. " 

2104 f"To create it by hand: {create_sql}" 

2105 ) 

2106 return 

2107 

2108 # Only now is the old index dead weight: it costs writes without ever 

2109 # serving the page query (PG's ASC default is NULLS LAST). 

2110 try: 

2111 await self.execute(f"DROP INDEX IF EXISTS {superseded_name}") 

2112 except Exception as drop_error: # pragma: no cover - best effort 

2113 logger.warning(f"Could not drop superseded scheduling index: {drop_error}") 

2114

2120 WHERE tablename = 'lightrag_doc_status' 

2121 AND indexname = $1 

2122 """, 

2123 [index_name], 

2124 ) 

2125 return bool(rows)

2169 async def _migrate_field_lengths(self): 

2170 """Migrate database field lengths: entity_name, source_id, target_id, and file_path""" 

2171 # Define the field changes needed 

2172 field_migrations = [ 

2173 { 

2174 "table": "LIGHTRAG_VDB_ENTITY", 

2175 "column": "entity_name", 

2176 "old_type": "character varying(255)", 

2177 "new_type": "VARCHAR(512)", 

2178 "description": "entity_name from 255 to 512", 

2179 }, 

2180 { 

2181 "table": "LIGHTRAG_VDB_RELATION", 

2182 "column": "source_id", 

2183 "old_type": "character varying(256)", 

2184 "new_type": "VARCHAR(512)", 

2185 "description": "source_id from 256 to 512", 

2186 }, 

2187 { 

2188 "table": "LIGHTRAG_VDB_RELATION", 

2189 "column": "target_id", 

2190 "old_type": "character varying(256)", 

2191 "new_type": "VARCHAR(512)", 

2192 "description": "target_id from 256 to 512", 

2193 }, 

2194 { 

2195 "table": "LIGHTRAG_DOC_CHUNKS", 

2196 "column": "file_path", 

2197 "old_type": "character varying(256)", 

2198 "new_type": "TEXT", 

2199 "description": "file_path to TEXT NULL", 

2200 }, 

2201 { 

2202 "table": "LIGHTRAG_VDB_CHUNKS", 

2203 "column": "file_path", 

2204 "old_type": "character varying(256)", 

2205 "new_type": "TEXT", 

2206 "description": "file_path to TEXT NULL", 

2207 }, 

2208 ] 

2209 

2210 try: 

2211 # Filter out tables that don't exist (e.g., legacy vector tables may not exist) 

2212 existing_migrations = [] 

2213 for migration in field_migrations: 

2214 if await self.check_table_exists(migration["table"]): 

2215 existing_migrations.append(migration) 

2216 else: 

2217 logger.debug( 

2218 f"Table {migration['table']} does not exist, skipping field length migration for {migration['column']}" 

2219 ) 

2220 

2221 # Skip if no migrations to process 

2222 if not existing_migrations: 

2223 logger.debug("No tables found for field length migration") 

2224 return 

2225 

2226 # Use filtered migrations for processing 

2227 field_migrations = existing_migrations 

2228 

2229 # Optimization: Batch check all columns in one query instead of 5 separate queries 

2230 unique_tables = list(set(m["table"].lower() for m in field_migrations)) 

2231 unique_columns = list(set(m["column"] for m in field_migrations)) 

2232 

2233 check_all_columns_sql = """ 

2234 SELECT table_name, column_name, data_type, character_maximum_length, is_nullable 

2235 FROM information_schema.columns 

2236 WHERE table_name = ANY($1) 

2237 AND column_name = ANY($2) 

2238 """ 

2239 

2240 all_columns_result = await self.query( 

2241 check_all_columns_sql, [unique_tables, unique_columns], multirows=True 

2242 ) 

2243 

2244 # Build lookup dict: (table_name, column_name) -> column_info 

2245 column_info_map = {} 

2246 if all_columns_result: 

2247 column_info_map = { 

2248 (row["table_name"].upper(), row["column_name"]): row 

2249 for row in all_columns_result 

2250 } 

2251 

2252 # Now iterate and migrate only what's needed 

2253 for migration in field_migrations: 

2254 try: 

2255 column_info = column_info_map.get( 

2256 (migration["table"], migration["column"]) 

2257 ) 

2258 

2259 if not column_info:

2827 asyncpg.exceptions.InvalidSchemaNameError, 

2828 ) as e: 

2829 if ignore_if_exists: 

2830 logger.debug("PostgreSQL, ignoring duplicate during execute: %r", e) 

2831 result = None 

2832 elif upsert: 

2833 logger.info( 

2834 "PostgreSQL, duplicate detected but treated as upsert success: %r", 

2835 e, 

2836 ) 

2837 result = None 

2838 else: 

2839 raise 

2840 except Exception: 

2841 if timing_label: 2841 ↛ 2847line 2841 didn't jump to line 2847 because the condition on line 2841 was always true

2842 performance_timing_log( 

2843 "[%s] connection.execute failed after %.4fs", 

2844 timing_label, 

2845 time.perf_counter() - execute_start, 

2846 ) 

2847 raise 

2848 if timing_label: 2848 ↛ 2855line 2848 didn't jump to line 2855 because the condition on line 2848 was always true

2849 performance_timing_log( 

2850 "[%s] connection.execute completed in %.4fs result=%s", 

2851 timing_label, 

2852 time.perf_counter() - execute_start, 

2853 result, 

2854 ) 

2855 return result 

2856 

2857 try: 

2858 await self._run_with_retry( 

2859 _operation, 

2860 with_age=with_age, 

2861 graph_name=graph_name, 

2862 timing_label=timing_label, 

2863 ) 

2864 except Exception as e: 

2865 logger.error(f"PostgreSQL database,\nsql:{sql},\ndata:{data},\nerror:{e}") 

2866 raise

2869class ClientManager:

3042 @classmethod 

3043 def _build_vector_signature( 

3044 cls, config: dict[str, Any], vector_storage: str | None 

3045 ) -> dict[str, Any]: 

3046 signature = { 

3047 "vector_storage": vector_storage, 

3048 "enable_vector": config["enable_vector"], 

3049 } 

3050 if config["enable_vector"]: 

3051 signature.update( 

3052 { 

3053 "vector_index_type": config["vector_index_type"], 

3054 "hnsw_m": config["hnsw_m"], 

3055 "hnsw_ef": config["hnsw_ef"], 

3056 "ivfflat_lists": config["ivfflat_lists"], 

3057 "vchordrq_build_options": config["vchordrq_build_options"], 

3058 "vchordrq_probes": config["vchordrq_probes"], 

3059 "vchordrq_epsilon": config["vchordrq_epsilon"], 

3060 } 

3061 ) 

3062 return signature 

3063 

3064 @classmethod 

3065 def _assert_compatible_vector_signature( 

3066 cls, requested_signature: dict[str, Any] 

3067 ) -> None: 

3068 active_signature = cls._instances["vector_signature"] 

3069 if active_signature is None or active_signature == requested_signature: 

3070 return 

3071 

3072 raise RuntimeError( 

3073 "PostgreSQL client pool is process-wide and already initialized with " 

3074 f"vector settings {active_signature}. Received incompatible settings " 

3075 f"{requested_signature}. Multiple LightRAG instances with different " 

3076 "PostgreSQL/vector storage configurations are not supported in the " 

3077 "same process." 

3078 ) 

3079 

3080 @classmethod 

3081 async def get_client(cls, vector_storage: str | None = None) -> PostgreSQLDB: 

3082 """Return the shared PostgreSQL client for all PG storages in this process. 

3083 

3084 The first caller fixes the vector-related pool configuration. Later calls 

3085 must provide a compatible vector storage setup or a RuntimeError is raised. 

3086 """ 

3087 async with cls._lock: 

3088 config = ClientManager.get_config(vector_storage=vector_storage) 

3089 requested_signature = cls._build_vector_signature(config, vector_storage) 

3090 if cls._instances["db"] is None: 

3091 db = PostgreSQLDB(config) 

3092 await db.initdb() 

3093 await db.check_tables() 

3094 cls._instances["db"] = db 

3095 cls._instances["ref_count"] = 0 

3096 cls._instances["vector_signature"] = requested_signature 

3097 else: 

3098 cls._assert_compatible_vector_signature(requested_signature) 

3099 cls._instances["ref_count"] += 1 

3100 return cls._instances["db"] 

3101 

3102 @classmethod 

3103 async def release_client(cls, db: PostgreSQLDB): 

3104 async with cls._lock: 

3105 if db is not None: 

3106 if db is cls._instances["db"]: 

3107 cls._instances["ref_count"] -= 1 

3108 if cls._instances["ref_count"] == 0: 

3109 if db.pool is not None: 

3110 await db.pool.close() 

3111 logger.info("Closed PostgreSQL database connection pool") 

3112 cls._instances["db"] = None 

3113 cls._instances["vector_signature"] = None 

3114 else: 

3115 if db.pool is not None: 

3116 await db.pool.close() 

3117 

3118

3306 async def get_by_id_strict(self, id: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:

3310 in this class swallows it), so a ``None`` from the legacy read is a 

3311 positively confirmed absence — safe for callers that take destructive

3326 def _order_results(

3329 """Preserve the caller requested ordering for bulk id lookups.""" 

3330 if not rows:

3332 

3333 id_map: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {} 

3334 for row in rows:

3337 row_id = row.get("id") 

3338 if row_id is not None:

3340 

3341 ordered: list[dict[str, Any] | None] = [] 

3342 for requested_id in ids: 

3343 ordered.append(id_map.get(str(requested_id))) 

3344 return ordered 

3345

3351 try: 

3352 llm_cache_list = json.loads(llm_cache_list)
