3357 heading = result.get("heading") 

3358 if isinstance(heading, str): 

3359 try: 

3360 heading = json.loads(heading) 

3361 except json.JSONDecodeError: 

3362 heading = {} 

3363 if not isinstance(heading, dict): 

3364 heading = {} 

3365 result["heading"] = heading 

3366 

3367 sidecar = result.get("sidecar") 

3368 if isinstance(sidecar, str): 

3369 try: 

3370 sidecar = json.loads(sidecar) 

3371 except json.JSONDecodeError: 

3372 sidecar = {} 

3373 if not isinstance(sidecar, dict): 

3374 sidecar = {} 

3375 result["sidecar"] = sidecar 

3376 

3377 create_time = result.get("create_time", 0) 

3378 update_time = result.get("update_time", 0) 

3379 result["create_time"] = create_time 

3380 result["update_time"] = create_time if update_time == 0 else update_time 

3381 

3382 if results and is_namespace(self.namespace, NameSpace.KV_STORE_FULL_DOCS): 

3383 for result in results: 

3384 chunk_options = result.get("chunk_options") 

3385 if isinstance(chunk_options, str): 

3386 try: 

3387 chunk_options = json.loads(chunk_options) 

3388 except json.JSONDecodeError: 

3389 chunk_options = {} 

3390 if not isinstance(chunk_options, dict): 

3391 chunk_options = {} 

3392 result["chunk_options"] = chunk_options

3395 if results and is_namespace( 

3396 self.namespace, NameSpace.KV_STORE_LLM_RESPONSE_CACHE 

3397 ): 

3398 processed_results = [] 

3399 for row in results: 

3400 create_time = row.get("create_time", 0) 

3401 update_time = row.get("update_time", 0) 

3402 # Parse queryparam JSON string back to dict 

3403 queryparam = row.get("queryparam") 

3404 if isinstance(queryparam, str): 

3405 try:

4595 async def upsert(self, data: dict[str, dict[str, Any]]) -> None: 

4596 """Buffer vector docs for embedding and batched flush. 

4597 

4598 Correctness premise: 

4599 LightRAG's pipeline is the normal write path for graph/vector 

4600 mutations and guarantees a single writer process per workspace. 

4601 This storage follows the same deferred-embedding contract as 

4602 OpenSearchVectorDBStorage: the pending buffer is process-local. 

4603 Committed PG rows are immediately visible across workers, but 

4604 *buffered* writes are not — readers in other workers will not 

4605 see them until the writing worker calls index_done_callback(). 

4606 

4607 Non-pipeline writers must provide equivalent single-writer 

4608 serialization and must flush explicitly before depending on 

4609 reads from another worker. 

4610 

4611 Memory expectation: 

4612 Pending docs (raw ``content`` strings, plus cached float32 

4613 vectors once embedded) accumulate in process memory until the 

4614 next ``index_done_callback()`` / ``finalize()``. This matches 

4615 the OpenSearch/Nano/Faiss contract. Callers performing very 

4616 large ingests should flush periodically (every N upserts) to 

4617 cap working-set size. 

4618 """ 

4619 if not data: 

4620 return 

4621 

4622 logger.debug( 

4623 f"[{self.workspace}] Buffering {len(data)} vectors for {self.namespace}" 

4624 ) 

4625 

4626 # Build pending docs outside the lock; UTC naive datetime mirrors 

4627 # the previous direct-write code path (the _upsert_* helpers feed 

4628 # this straight into asyncpg as a timestamp). 

4629 current_time = datetime.datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None) 

4630 pending_docs: list[tuple[str, _PendingPGVectorDoc]] = [] 

4631 for i, (k, v) in enumerate(data.items(), start=1): 

4632 pending_docs.append( 

4633 ( 

4634 k, 

4635 _PendingPGVectorDoc( 

4636 item={"__id__": k, **v}, 

4637 created_at=current_time, 

4638 ), 

4639 ) 

4640 ) 

4641 await _cooperative_yield(i) 

4642 

4643 async with self._flush_lock: 

4644 for doc_id, pending_doc in pending_docs: 

4645 # Invariant: a later upsert wins over an earlier delete; the 

4646 # unconditional dict assignment also discards any cached 

4647 # stale vector from a prior upsert of the same id. 

4648 self._pending_vector_deletes.discard(doc_id) 

4649 self._pending_vector_docs[doc_id] = pending_doc

5052 async def delete_entity_relation(self, entity_name: str) -> None:

5367 async def drop(self) -> dict[str, str]: 

5368 """Drop all rows scoped to this storage's workspace. 

5369 

5370 The underlying table is shared across workspaces and is NOT 

5371 dropped — this method issues ``DELETE FROM <table> WHERE 

5372 workspace=$1`` and clears the pending buffers (queued 

5373 upserts/deletes against rows that are about to disappear are 

5374 meaningless). 

5375 

5376 The same workspace-scoped delete is also issued against the kept 

5377 legacy table (the un-suffixed table that the model-suffix 

5378 migration leaves behind as a backup), when it still exists. The 

5379 legacy->suffixed migration only runs while the suffixed table has 

5380 no rows for the workspace; if a deliberate clear left this 

5381 workspace's data behind in legacy, the next startup would migrate 

5382 it back into the freshly-emptied suffixed table (resurrection). 

5383 Only this workspace's legacy rows are removed, so other 

5384 workspaces' legacy data and their pending one-time migration stay 

5385 intact. 

5386 

5387 Callable on an instance whose ``initialize()`` refused with 

5388 ``VectorSpaceMismatchError``: that is the recovery 

5389 `lightrag-rebuild-vdb` performs, and it converges because the 

5390 legacy cleanup above removes the very rows the refusal was about. 

5391 

5392 Concurrency contract: 

5393 ``_flush_lock`` guards same-process flush / upsert / delete 

5394 races only. Cross-worker buffered writes are NOT covered — 

5395 another worker's pending buffer can flush stale rows back 

5396 into the table immediately after this call returns. Callers 

5397 running inside the LightRAG framework MUST hold 

5398 ``pipeline_status["destructive_busy"] = True`` (acquired 

5399 atomically via ``_acquire_destructive_busy``) for the entire 

5400 duration of the drop; the ``/documents/clear`` endpoint 

5401 already does this before invoking ``drop()`` on every 

5402 storage. Direct callers (tests, ops scripts, debugging) are 

5403 responsible for ensuring no other writer is touching this 

5404 workspace. 

5405 

5406 Returns: 

5407 ``{"status": "success" | "error", "message": ...}``. Unlike 

5408 ``delete()`` / ``delete_entity()`` / ``delete_entity_relation()`` 

5409 which re-raise on failure, ``drop()`` swallows the exception 

5410 into the return dict — callers MUST inspect ``status`` to 

5411 detect failure. The exception is also logged at ``error`` 

5412 level so a missed status check still leaves a trail. 

5413 """ 

5414 try: 

5415 async with self._flush_lock: 

5416 self._pending_vector_docs.clear() 

5417 self._pending_vector_deletes.clear() 

5418 # The suffixed table may legitimately not exist: an 

5419 # initialize() that refused with VectorSpaceMismatchError raised 

5420 # BEFORE creating it, and that refusal is exactly what 

5421 # `lightrag-rebuild-vdb` calls this method to clear. Nothing to 

5422 # delete there is success, not an error -- the legacy cleanup 

5423 # below is the part that actually clears the refusal. 

5424 if await self.db.check_table_exists(self.table_name): 

5425 drop_sql = SQL_TEMPLATES["drop_specifiy_table_workspace"].format( 

5426 table_name=self.table_name 

5427 ) 

5428 await self.db.execute(drop_sql, {"workspace": self.workspace}) 

5429 

5430 # Also clear this workspace's rows from the kept legacy table so 

5431 # the next startup does not re-migrate the just-cleared data 

5432 # back into the suffixed table. Skip when there is no separate 

5433 # legacy table (no model suffix) or it no longer exists. 

5434 if ( 

5435 self.legacy_table_name 

5436 and self.legacy_table_name.lower() != self.table_name.lower() 

5437 and await self.db.check_table_exists(self.legacy_table_name) 

5438 ): 

5439 legacy_drop_sql = SQL_TEMPLATES[ 

5440 "drop_specifiy_table_workspace" 

5441 ].format(table_name=self.legacy_table_name) 

5442 await self.db.execute( 

5443 legacy_drop_sql, {"workspace": self.workspace} 

5444 ) 

5445 return {"status": "success", "message": "data dropped"} 

5446 except Exception as e: 

5447 logger.error( 

5448 f"[{self.workspace}] Error dropping vector storage " 

5449 f"{self.namespace}: {e}" 

5450 ) 

5451 return {"status": "error", "message": str(e)}

5747 async def get_doc_by_file_basename( 

5748 self, basename: str 

5749 ) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any]] | None: 

5750 """PG-native override of basename-based document lookup. 

5751 

5752 Replaces the base-class full-table scan with a database-level query on 

5753 the canonical ``file_path`` column. The caller is responsible for 

5754 passing an already-canonical basename; storage performs an exact match 

5755 only. 

5756 

5757 ``file_path`` is one-to-many (duplicate-attempt ``dup-*`` rows keep the 

5758 same canonical basename); this returns the single PRIMARY 

5759 (``metadata.is_duplicate != true``) row — callers doing identity checks 

5760 / dedup want the document, never a duplicate marker. When only 

5761 duplicate markers remain (primary deleted) the basename is free again 

5762 and this returns ``None``. 

5763 """ 

5764 if not basename: 

5765 return None 

5766 

5767 if basename == "unknown_source": 

5768 return None 

5769 

5770 # COALESCE((metadata->>'is_duplicate')::boolean, false) excludes 

5771 # duplicate-marker rows; NULL/absent metadata keys coalesce to false 

5772 # (primary). metadata is JSONB, so ->> yields 'true'/'false' text that 

5773 # casts cleanly; a non-boolean value raises and propagates (fail 

5774 # closed) rather than silently matching.

5776 "SELECT * FROM LIGHTRAG_DOC_STATUS " 

5777 "WHERE workspace=$1 AND file_path = $2 " 

5778 "AND COALESCE((metadata->>'is_duplicate')::boolean, false) = false " 

5779 "ORDER BY created_at ASC, id ASC LIMIT 1" 

5780 ) 

5781 params = [self.workspace, basename] 

5782 

5783 result = await self.db.query(sql, params, True) 

5784 if not result: 

5785 return None 

5786 row = result[0] 

5787 

5788 chunks_list = row.get("chunks_list", []) 

5789 if isinstance(chunks_list, str): 5789 ↛ 5795line 5789 didn't jump to line 5795 because the condition on line 5789 was always true

5790 try: 

5791 chunks_list = json.loads(chunks_list) 

5792 except json.JSONDecodeError: 

5793 chunks_list = [] 

5794 

5795 metadata = row.get("metadata", {}) 

5796 if isinstance(metadata, str): 5796 ↛ 5802line 5796 didn't jump to line 5802 because the condition on line 5796 was always true

5797 try: 

5798 metadata = json.loads(metadata) 

5799 except json.JSONDecodeError: 

5800 metadata = {} 

5801 

5802 created_at = self._format_datetime_with_timezone(row["created_at"]) 

5803 updated_at = self._format_datetime_with_timezone(row["updated_at"]) 

5804

5821 async def get_doc_by_content_hash( 

5822 self, content_hash: str, *, exclude_doc_id: str | None = None 

5823 ) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any]] | None: 

5824 """PG-native override of content-hash document lookup. 

5825 

5826 Replaces the base-class full-table scan with an indexed query on 

5827 ``workspace + content_hash``. Empty strings are treated as a miss 

5828 to align with the partial-index predicate. ``exclude_doc_id`` adds an 

5829 indexed ``AND id != $3`` plus a jsonb predicate dropping any row that 

5830 merely POINTS at that id (``is_duplicate`` naming it as 

5831 ``original_doc_id``), so the duplicate check gets the earliest holder 

5832 that is neither the row being processed nor a record of it, in one 

5833 bounded query (see base contract). Both are WHERE predicates on the same 

5834 indexed scan, so skipping a pointer row cannot truncate the search — 

5835 ``LIMIT 1`` still returns the earliest row that survives them. 

5836 """ 

5837 if not content_hash: 

5838 return None 

5839 

5840 params: list[Any] = [self.workspace, content_hash] 

5841 exclude_clause = "" 

5842 if exclude_doc_id is not None: 

5843 params.append(exclude_doc_id) 

5844 # Same ``(metadata->>'is_duplicate')::boolean`` reading as 

5845 # ``_PRIMARY_PREDICATE`` — one interpretation of that flag per 

5846 # backend, and a non-boolean value raises (fail closed) instead of 

5847 # silently deciding. ``original_doc_id`` is COALESCEd because a NULL 

5848 # would make the whole NOT(...) NULL, and a WHERE that is NULL drops 

5849 # the row — filtering out a duplicate marker that recorded no 

5850 # original, which is not what this excludes. 

5851 exclude_clause = ( 

5852 f" AND id <> ${len(params)} AND NOT (" 

5853 "COALESCE((metadata->>'is_duplicate')::boolean, false) " 

5854 f"AND COALESCE(metadata->>'original_doc_id', '') = ${len(params)})" 

5855 ) 

5856 sql = ( 

5857 "SELECT * FROM LIGHTRAG_DOC_STATUS " 

5858 f"WHERE workspace=$1 AND content_hash=$2{exclude_clause} " 

5859 "ORDER BY created_at ASC, id ASC LIMIT 1" 

5860 ) 

5861 result = await self.db.query(sql, params, True) 

5862 if not result: 

5863 return None 

5864 row = result[0] 

5865 

5866 chunks_list = row.get("chunks_list", []) 

5867 if isinstance(chunks_list, str): 5867 ↛ 5873line 5867 didn't jump to line 5873 because the condition on line 5867 was always true

5868 try: 

5869 chunks_list = json.loads(chunks_list) 

5870 except json.JSONDecodeError: 

5871 chunks_list = [] 

5872 

5873 metadata = row.get("metadata", {}) 

5874 if isinstance(metadata, str): 5874 ↛ 5880line 5874 didn't jump to line 5880 because the condition on line 5874 was always true

5875 try: 

5876 metadata = json.loads(metadata) 

5877 except json.JSONDecodeError: 

5878 metadata = {} 

5879 

5880 created_at = self._format_datetime_with_timezone(row["created_at"]) 

5881 updated_at = self._format_datetime_with_timezone(row["updated_at"]) 

5882 

5883 doc = dict( 

5884 content_length=row["content_length"], 

5885 content_summary=row["content_summary"], 

5886 status=row["status"], 

5887 chunks_count=row["chunks_count"], 

5888 created_at=created_at, 

5889 updated_at=updated_at, 

5890 file_path=row["file_path"], 

5891 chunks_list=chunks_list,

5894 track_id=row.get("track_id"), 

5895 content_hash=row.get("content_hash"), 

5896 ) 

5897 return str(row["id"]), doc 

5898 

5899 # SQL predicate isolating PRIMARY (non-duplicate) rows. metadata is JSONB, 

5900 # so ->> yields 'true'/'false' text that casts cleanly; a NULL/absent key 

5901 # coalesces to false (primary), and a non-boolean value raises and 

5902 # propagates (fail closed) rather than silently matching. 

5903 _PRIMARY_PREDICATE = "COALESCE((metadata->>'is_duplicate')::boolean, false) = false"

5905 async def resolve_doc_source_strict( 

5906 self, canonical_source_key: str 

5907 ) -> SourceResolution: 

5908 """Typed, conflict-aware source resolution (see base contract). 

5909 

5910 Fetches up to two PRIMARY rows for the canonical basename and maps 

5911 0/1/≥2 → Absent/Unique/Conflict. When two are found the exact count is 

5912 an indexed ``COUNT(*)`` on the same predicate. Every asyncpg 

5913 transport/server error propagates out of ``db.query`` (nothing here 

5914 swallows it), so a returned ``SourceAbsent`` IS a confirmed absence. 

5915 """ 

5916 if not canonical_source_key or canonical_source_key == "unknown_source": 

5917 return SourceAbsent() 

5918 

5919 sql = ( 

5920 "SELECT id, status, created_at, updated_at, file_path, track_id, " 

5921 "metadata FROM LIGHTRAG_DOC_STATUS " 

5922 "WHERE workspace=$1 AND file_path=$2 " 

5923 f"AND {self._PRIMARY_PREDICATE} " 

5924 "ORDER BY created_at ASC, id ASC LIMIT 2" 

5925 ) 

5926 rows = await self.db.query(sql, [self.workspace, canonical_source_key], True) 

5927 if not rows: 

5928 return SourceAbsent() 

5929 if len(rows) == 1: 

5930 row = rows[0] 

5931 return SourceUnique( 

5932 doc_id=str(row["id"]), 

5933 doc=self._pg_scheduling_record_from_row(row, strict=True), 

5934 ) 

5935 # ≥2 primary candidates: exact count is cheap on the indexed predicate. 

5936 count_row = await self.db.query( 

5937 "SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM LIGHTRAG_DOC_STATUS " 

5938 "WHERE workspace=$1 AND file_path=$2 " 

5939 f"AND {self._PRIMARY_PREDICATE}", 

5940 [self.workspace, canonical_source_key], 

5941 ) 

5942 candidate_count = int(count_row["c"]) if count_row else None 

5943 return SourceConflict( 

5944 candidate_count=candidate_count, 

5945 sample_doc_ids=tuple(sorted(str(r["id"]) for r in rows)), 

5946 )

5960 @staticmethod 

5961 def _decode_cursor(opaque: str) -> tuple[datetime.datetime | None, str]: 

5962 """Decode an opaque page cursor into (created_at, id). 

5963 

5964 The opaque form is ``json.dumps([created_at_iso | None, id])`` 

5965 produced by ``_encode_cursor``. A ``None`` first element marks the 

5966 NULL-created_at bucket (corrupt rows, sorted FIRST — see the page 

5967 docstring); a string round-trips exactly through 

5968 ``datetime.fromisoformat`` (microseconds preserved) and is normalized 

5969 back to the naive-UTC form the TIMESTAMP column stores, so the 

5970 parameterized row-value comparison resumes at exactly the last 

5971 consumed key. A malformed cursor raises 

5972 :class:`~lightrag.exceptions.StorageControlPlaneError`. 

5973 """ 

5974 try: 

5975 decoded = json.loads(opaque) 

5976 created_iso, doc_id = decoded 

5977 if not isinstance(doc_id, str): 

5978 raise ValueError("cursor id must be a string") 

5979 if created_iso is None: 

5980 return None, doc_id 

5981 if not isinstance(created_iso, str): 

5982 raise ValueError("cursor created_at must be a string or null") 

5983 created = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(created_iso) 

5984 except (ValueError, TypeError) as e: 

5985 raise StorageControlPlaneError( 

5986 f"Malformed scheduling cursor for PGDocStatusStorage: {e}" 

5987 ) from e 

5988 if created.tzinfo is not None: 

5989 created = created.astimezone(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None) 

5990 return created, doc_id 

5991 

5992 def _encode_cursor(self, row: dict[str, Any]) -> str: 

5993 """Encode the keyset key of a returned DB row as an opaque cursor. 

5994 

5995 Rows with a NULL created_at (corrupt writes — the column defaults to 

5996 CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) sort FIRST and encode as ``[null, id]`` so the 

5997 sweep traverses past them instead of losing them behind a row-value 

5998 comparison that NULL can never satisfy (matching the JSON/Redis 

5999 backends, which sort a missing created_at first as "").""" 

6000 created = row.get("created_at") 

6001 if not isinstance(created, datetime.datetime): 

6002 return json.dumps([None, str(row["id"])]) 

6003 return json.dumps( 

6004 [self._format_datetime_with_timezone(created), str(row["id"])] 

6005 ) 

6006

6051 async def get_docs_by_statuses_page( 

6052 self, 

6053 statuses: list[DocStatus], 

6054 *, 

6055 limit: int, 

6056 position: CursorPosition = CURSOR_START, 

6057 strict: bool = False, 

6058 ) -> DocStatusPage: 

6059 """Bounded keyset page over LIGHTRAG_DOC_STATUS. 

6060 

6061 **One parenthesised branch per status, UNION ALL'd**, each carrying the 

6062 same keyset predicate, the same ``ORDER BY created_at ASC NULLS FIRST, 

6063 id ASC`` and the same ``LIMIT``; the wrapper re-sorts and re-limits. That 

6064 shape is what lets the planner MergeAppend ordered index scans on 

6065 ``idx_lightrag_doc_status_ws_status_created_nf_id``. 

6066 

6067 It replaced a single ``status = ANY($2)`` query, which read as if the 

6068 planner would combine per-status index ranges under the LIMIT. Measured 

6069 instead, on 60k rows: one status was a bitmap scan plus a top-N sort of 

6070 7583 rows, and TWO statuses — the AUTO sweep's own shape — was a full 

6071 ``Seq Scan`` of the table plus a sort, every page. Page *memory* was 

6072 bounded (top-N heapsort keeps ``limit`` rows), so the RSS claim held, but 

6073 the I/O was O(table) per page, making a full sweep O(n²/page_size). 

6074 With the branch form the same two-status page is an ordered index scan 

6075 touching 501 rows, 14.8ms → 0.29ms. 

6076 

6077 The consumed-frontier rules survive the rewrite. ``next_position`` is the 

6078 last RETURNED row's key: an unreturned row is either one of the fetched 

6079 rows outside the top-``limit`` window (so above the frontier), or beyond 

6080 a branch that hit its own LIMIT — and that branch's last fetched row is 

6081 itself ≥ the frontier, since otherwise all of its rows would have fitted 

6082 in the window. ``returned < limit`` still proves exhaustion, because the 

6083 union can only be short when every branch was short. 

6084 

6085 Consumed-position contract (SQL-side filtering makes it trivial): 

6086 every predicate — workspace and status membership — is part of the DB 

6087 scan itself, so the database skips non-matching rows and keeps scanning 

6088 until LIMIT rows are collected or the keyset range ends. The rows 

6089 returned by the query therefore ARE the consumed frontier: 

6090 

6091 * ``next_position`` = key of the LAST RETURNED row, and 

6092 * ``returned < limit`` proves the (unfiltered) keyset range is 

6093 exhausted — the scan only stops early when the range ends, so a 

6094 short page can never hide rows that were merely filtered out 

6095 (unlike client-side filtering, where a fully-filtered page must 

6096 still advance without terminating). 

6097 

6098 ``strict=True``: any DB error or row-conversion failure raises without 

6099 returning partial docs or a cursor (single round-trip — there is no 

6100 partial-page surface). In relaxed mode an unusable row is skipped from 

6101 the projection but stays consumed (it was returned by the scan). 

6102 

6103 NULL created_at (corrupt writes): such rows sort FIRST 

6104 (``NULLS FIRST``, mirroring JSON/Redis where a missing created_at 

6105 sorts first as "") and the keyset comparison is bucket-aware — a 

6106 plain ``(created_at, id) > ($c, $i)`` row-value comparison evaluates 

6107 to NULL for them, which would silently starve them out of every page 

6108 after the first, violating the strict complete-or-raise promise. 

6109 They therefore stay reachable: raised under strict, skipped (but 

6110 consumed) under relaxed. 

6111 """ 

6112 if limit <= 0: 

6113 raise ValueError(f"page limit must be positive, got {limit}") 

6114 if not statuses or position is CURSOR_END: 

6115 return DocStatusPage(docs={}, next_position=CURSOR_END) 

6116 

6117 params: list[Any] = [self.workspace] 

6118 

6119 # The keyset predicate is identical in every branch; build it once. 

6120 cursor_sql = "" 

6121 if isinstance(position, CursorAfter): 

6122 cur_created, cur_id = self._decode_cursor(position.opaque) 

6123 if cur_created is None: 

6124 # Cursor inside the NULL bucket (sorted first): continue 

6125 # through the remaining NULL rows by id, then everything 

6126 # with a real timestamp. 

6127 params.append(cur_id) 

6128 cursor_sql = ( 

6129 f" AND ((created_at IS NULL AND id > ${len(params)}) " 

6130 "OR created_at IS NOT NULL)" 

6131 ) 

6132 else: 

6133 # Past the NULL bucket: only real-timestamp rows can follow. 

6134 params.append(cur_created) 

6135 params.append(cur_id) 

6136 cursor_sql = ( 

6137 " AND created_at IS NOT NULL AND " 

6138 f"(created_at, id) > (${len(params) - 1}::timestamp, " 

6139 f"${len(params)})" 

6140 ) 

6141 params.append(limit) 

6142 limit_param = len(params) 

6143 

6144 order_by = "ORDER BY created_at ASC NULLS FIRST, id ASC" 

6145 branches: list[str] = [] 

6146 for status in statuses: 

6147 params.append(status.value) 

6148 branches.append( 

6149 "(SELECT id, status, created_at, updated_at, file_path, " 

6150 "track_id, metadata FROM LIGHTRAG_DOC_STATUS " 

6151 f"WHERE workspace=$1 AND status=${len(params)}{cursor_sql} " 

6152 f"{order_by} LIMIT ${limit_param})" 

6153 ) 

6154 if len(branches) == 1: 

6155 sql = branches[0] 

6156 else: 

6157 sql = ( 

6158 f"SELECT * FROM ({' UNION ALL '.join(branches)}) u " 

6159 f"{order_by} LIMIT ${limit_param}" 

6160 ) 

6161 

6162 # Any asyncpg error propagates out of db.query — strict pages never 

6163 # commit a new cursor on failure. 

6164 rows = await self.db.query(sql, params, multirows=True) or [] 

6165 

6166 docs: dict[str, DocSchedulingRecord] = {} 

6167 for row in rows: 

6168 record = self._pg_scheduling_record_from_row(row, strict=strict) 

6169 if record is None: 

6170 continue # relaxed skip is still consumed (see docstring) 

6171 docs[record.id] = record 

6172 

6173 if len(rows) < limit: 

6174 next_position: CursorPosition = CURSOR_END 

6175 else: 

6176 next_position = CursorAfter(self._encode_cursor(rows[-1])) 

6177 return DocStatusPage(docs=docs, next_position=next_position)

6179 async def count_docs_by_statuses( 

6180 self, statuses: list[DocStatus], *, strict: bool = True 

6181 ) -> int: 

6182 """Fail-closed status count: an accurate number or an exception. 

6183 

6184 Unlike ``get_status_counts`` implementations that swallow errors, 

6185 every DB failure propagates — admission control treats an error as 

6186 "refuse", never as "capacity available". 

6187 """ 

6188 if not statuses: 

6189 return 0 

6190 sql = ( 

6191 'SELECT COUNT(*) AS "count" FROM LIGHTRAG_DOC_STATUS ' 

6192 "WHERE workspace=$1 AND status = ANY($2)" 

6193 )

6195 if row is None or row.get("count") is None: 

6196 raise StorageControlPlaneError( 

6197 f"[{self.workspace}] COUNT query returned no row for " 

6198 "count_docs_by_statuses; refusing to report a count" 

6199 ) 

6200 return int(row["count"])

6213 async def update_doc_status_fields( 

6214 self, 

6215 doc_id: str, 

6216 fields: dict[str, Any], 

6217 *, 

6218 missing_ok: bool = False, 

6219 ) -> None:

6232 )

6242 "SELECT id FROM LIGHTRAG_DOC_STATUS WHERE workspace=$1 AND id=$2", 

6243 [self.workspace, doc_id],

6254 sql = ( 

6255 "UPDATE LIGHTRAG_DOC_STATUS SET " 

6256 + ", ".join(set_clauses) 

6257 + " WHERE workspace=$1 AND id=$2 RETURNING id" 

6258 )

6260 if row is None: 

6261 if missing_ok: 

6262 return

6312 -> :class:`DocProcessingStatus` normalisation as

6341 # ------------------------------------------------------------------ 

6342 # Source-conflict listing and explicit CAS repair 

6343 # ------------------------------------------------------------------ 

6344 

6345 @staticmethod 

6346 def _conflict_fingerprint(sorted_doc_ids: list[str]) -> str: 

6347 """Deterministic digest over candidate doc IDs in stable sort order.""" 

6348 digest = hashlib.sha256() 

6349 for doc_id in sorted_doc_ids: 

6350 digest.update(doc_id.encode("utf-8")) 

6351 digest.update(b"\x00") 

6352 return digest.hexdigest() 

6353 

6354 @staticmethod 

6355 def _decode_conflict_cursor(opaque: str) -> str: 

6356 try: 

6357 key = json.loads(opaque) 

6358 if not isinstance(key, str): 

6359 raise ValueError("conflict cursor must be a string") 

6360 except (ValueError, TypeError) as e: 

6361 raise StorageControlPlaneError( 

6362 f"Malformed source-conflict cursor for PGDocStatusStorage: {e}" 

6363 ) from e 

6364 return key 

6365 

6366 async def list_source_conflicts_page( 

6367 self, 

6368 *, 

6369 limit: int, 

6370 position: CursorPosition = CURSOR_START, 

6371 ) -> SourceConflictPage: 

6372 """Page canonical source keys with >1 primary candidate (see base). 

6373 

6374 ``GROUP BY file_path HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2`` over PRIMARY rows only, 

6375 keyset-ordered by the canonical key so pages are stable and bounded. 

6376 Each key's bounded sample is fetched with its own ``ORDER BY id LIMIT 

6377 _CONFLICT_SAMPLE_CAP`` query, so no group ever materializes its whole 

6378 candidate set. 

6379 """ 

6380 if limit <= 0: 

6381 raise ValueError(f"page limit must be positive, got {limit}") 

6382 if position is CURSOR_END: 

6383 return SourceConflictPage(conflicts=(), next_position=CURSOR_END) 

6384 params: list[Any] = [self.workspace] 

6385 sql = ( 

6386 "SELECT file_path, COUNT(*) AS c FROM LIGHTRAG_DOC_STATUS " 

6387 f"WHERE workspace=$1 AND {self._PRIMARY_PREDICATE} " 

6388 "AND file_path IS NOT NULL " 

6389 "AND file_path NOT IN ('', 'unknown_source', 'no-file-path')" 

6390 ) 

6391 if isinstance(position, CursorAfter): 

6392 params.append(self._decode_conflict_cursor(position.opaque)) 

6393 sql += f" AND file_path > ${len(params)}" 

6394 params.append(limit) 

6395 sql += ( 

6396 " GROUP BY file_path HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 " 

6397 f"ORDER BY file_path ASC LIMIT ${len(params)}" 

6398 ) 

6399 rows = await self.db.query(sql, params, multirows=True) or [] 

6400 

6401 conflicts: list[SourceConflictSummary] = [] 

6402 for row in rows: 

6403 key = row["file_path"] 

6404 sample = ( 

6405 await self.db.query( 

6406 "SELECT id FROM LIGHTRAG_DOC_STATUS " 

6407 f"WHERE workspace=$1 AND file_path=$2 AND {self._PRIMARY_PREDICATE} " 

6408 "ORDER BY id ASC LIMIT $3", 

6409 [self.workspace, key, self._CONFLICT_SAMPLE_CAP], 

6410 multirows=True, 

6411 ) 

6412 or [] 

6413 ) 

6414 conflicts.append( 

6415 SourceConflictSummary( 

6416 canonical_source_key=key, 

6417 candidate_count=int(row["c"]), 

6418 sample_doc_ids=tuple(str(r["id"]) for r in sample), 

6419 ) 

6420 ) 

6421 

6422 if len(rows) < limit: 

6423 next_position: CursorPosition = CURSOR_END 

6424 else: 

6425 next_position = CursorAfter( 

6426 json.dumps(rows[-1]["file_path"], ensure_ascii=False) 

6427 ) 

6428 return SourceConflictPage( 

6429 conflicts=tuple(conflicts), next_position=next_position 

6430 ) 

6431 

6432 async def repair_source_conflict( 

6433 self, 

6434 canonical_source_key: str, 

6435 *, 

6436 primary_doc_id: str, 

6437 expected_candidate_count: int, 

6438 expected_candidate_fingerprint: str, 

6439 dry_run: bool = True, 

6440 ) -> SourceConflictRepairResult: 

6441 """Demote all-but-one primary to duplicate, CAS-guarded (see base). 

6442 

6443 The candidate set is re-read ``FOR UPDATE`` inside ONE transaction, so 

6444 the count/fingerprint recomputation, the CAS check and the demotions 

6445 are atomic with respect to the rows it SAW. ``FOR UPDATE`` takes no 

6446 predicate lock, so it cannot block a new primary being INSERTED for the 

6447 same canonical key mid-repair — see the base contract for what 

6448 ``committed`` does and does not claim, and for the caller-side locks 

6449 that serialize repair against enqueue. dry-run reports the current 

6450 count/fingerprint without mutating; commit refuses 

6451 (:class:`SourceConflictRepairCASError`) when they no longer match the 

6452 operator-echoed expectation. Losing candidates get 

6453 ``metadata.is_duplicate=true`` + ``original_doc_id=primary_doc_id`` in 

6454 the same transaction; content is never deleted. ``primary_doc_id`` not 

6455 in the current candidate set raises ``ValueError``. 

6456 """ 

6457 workspace = self.workspace 

6458 predicate = self._PRIMARY_PREDICATE 

6459 sample_cap = self._CONFLICT_SAMPLE_CAP 

6460 

6461 async def _repair( 

6462 connection: asyncpg.Connection, 

6463 ) -> SourceConflictRepairResult: 

6464 async with connection.transaction(): 

6465 rows = await connection.fetch( 

6466 "SELECT id FROM LIGHTRAG_DOC_STATUS " 

6467 f"WHERE workspace=$1 AND file_path=$2 AND {predicate} " 

6468 "ORDER BY id ASC FOR UPDATE", 

6469 workspace, 

6470 canonical_source_key, 

6471 ) 

6472 candidates = sorted(str(r["id"]) for r in rows) 

6473 count = len(candidates) 

6474 fingerprint = self._conflict_fingerprint(candidates) 

6475 if primary_doc_id not in candidates: 

6476 raise ValueError( 

6477 f"primary_doc_id {primary_doc_id!r} is not a current " 

6478 f"primary candidate for {canonical_source_key!r}" 

6479 ) 

6480 demoted = [d for d in candidates if d != primary_doc_id] 

6481 if dry_run: 

6482 return SourceConflictRepairResult( 

6483 canonical_source_key=canonical_source_key, 

6484 primary_doc_id=primary_doc_id, 

6485 candidate_count=count, 

6486 fingerprint=fingerprint, 

6487 demoted_sample_doc_ids=tuple(demoted[:sample_cap]), 

6488 committed=False, 

6489 ) 

6490 if ( 

6491 count != expected_candidate_count 

6492 or fingerprint != expected_candidate_fingerprint 

6493 ): 

6494 raise SourceConflictRepairCASError( 

6495 f"[{workspace}] source-conflict repair CAS failed for " 

6496 f"{canonical_source_key!r}: candidate set changed " 

6497 f"(count {count} vs {expected_candidate_count})" 

6498 ) 

6499 if demoted: 6499 ↛ 6513line 6499 didn't jump to line 6513 because the condition on line 6499 was always true

6500 # jsonb_set both keys, coalescing a NULL/missing metadata 

6501 # to '{}' first; the derived is_duplicate exclusion updates 

6502 # in the same transaction as the row rewrite. 

6503 await connection.execute( 

6504 "UPDATE LIGHTRAG_DOC_STATUS SET metadata = jsonb_set(" 

6505 "jsonb_set(COALESCE(metadata, '{}'::jsonb), " 

6506 "'{is_duplicate}', 'true'::jsonb, true), " 

6507 "'{original_doc_id}', to_jsonb($3::text), true) " 

6508 "WHERE workspace=$1 AND id = ANY($2)", 

6509 workspace, 

6510 demoted, 

6511 primary_doc_id, 

6512 ) 

6513 return SourceConflictRepairResult( 

6514 canonical_source_key=canonical_source_key, 

6515 primary_doc_id=primary_doc_id, 

6516 candidate_count=count, 

6517 fingerprint=fingerprint, 

6518 demoted_sample_doc_ids=tuple(demoted[:sample_cap]), 

6519 committed=True, 

6520 ) 

6521 

6522 return await self.db._run_with_retry(_repair) 

6523

6650 self,

6652 status_filters: list[DocStatus] | None = None,

6677 performance_timing_log( 

6678 "[%s] PGDocStatusStorage.get_docs_paginated start status_filter=%s page=%s page_size=%s sort_field=%s sort_direction=%s", 

6679 self.workspace, 

6680 status_filter_value, 

6681 page, 

6682 page_size, 

6683 sort_field, 

6684 sort_direction, 

6685 ) 

6686 

6687 # Validate parameters 

6688 if page < 1: 

6689 page = 1 

6690 if page_size < 10: 

6691 page_size = 10 

6692 elif page_size > 200: 

6693 page_size = 200 

6694 

6695 # Whitelist validation for sort_field to prevent SQL injection 

6696 allowed_sort_fields = {"created_at", "updated_at", "id", "file_path"} 

6697 if sort_field not in allowed_sort_fields: 

6698 sort_field = "updated_at" 

6699 

6700 # Whitelist validation for sort_direction to prevent SQL injection 

6701 if sort_direction.lower() not in ["asc", "desc"]: 

6702 sort_direction = "desc" 

6703 else: 

6704 sort_direction = sort_direction.lower() 

6705 

6706 # Calculate offset 

6707 offset = (page - 1) * page_size 

6708 

6709 # Build parameterized query components 

6710 params = {"workspace": self.workspace} 

6711 param_count = 1 

6712 

6713 # Build WHERE clause with parameterized query 

6714 if status_filter_values is not None: 

6715 param_count += 1 

6716 where_clause = "WHERE workspace=$1 AND status = ANY($2)" 

6717 params["status_filters"] = sorted(status_filter_values) 

6718 else: 

6719 where_clause = "WHERE workspace=$1" 

6720 

6721 # Build ORDER BY clause using validated whitelist values. 

6722 # NULLS LAST is applied in both the inner paged CTE and the outer query so 

6723 # that the LIMIT/OFFSET slice boundary and the display order are identical. 

6724 # Without it, DESC defaults to NULLS FIRST: nulls land on earlier pages but 

6725 # are re-sorted to the end by the outer ORDER BY, dropping non-null rows. 

6726 order_clause = f"ORDER BY {sort_field} {sort_direction.upper()} NULLS LAST" 

6727 

6728 # Two-CTE query: total count + page data in a single round-trip. 

6729 # 

6730 # COUNT(*) OVER () was replaced because when the LIMIT/OFFSET clause yields 

6731 # no rows (out-of-range page), there are no result rows to carry the window 

6732 # function value — so total_count would not appear in the output at all, 

6733 # making it impossible to distinguish "0 matching documents" from "non-empty 

6734 # result set, page is past the end". 

6735 # 

6736 # The LEFT JOIN pattern fixes this: the `total` CTE always produces exactly 

6737 # one row (the aggregate count over the full WHERE clause), and the outer 

6738 # LEFT JOIN emits that one row even when `paged` is empty. Python then 

6739 # skips rows where id IS NULL (the empty-page sentinel). 

6740 # 

6741 # chunks_list is intentionally excluded from the paged CTE SELECT list: 

6742 # DocStatusResponse does not expose it, so transferring the full JSONB array 

6743 # would be pure overhead. The chunks_list=[] in the constructor below is 

6744 # intentional — see the paged CTE column list above. 

6745 params["limit"] = page_size 

6746 params["offset"] = offset 

6747 cte_sql = f""" 

6748 WITH total AS ( 

6749 SELECT COUNT(*) AS _total_count 

6750 FROM LIGHTRAG_DOC_STATUS 

6751 {where_clause} 

6752 ), 

6753 paged AS ( 

6754 SELECT id, workspace, content_summary, content_length, chunks_count, 

6755 status, file_path, track_id, metadata, error_msg, content_hash, 

6756 created_at, updated_at 

6757 FROM LIGHTRAG_DOC_STATUS 

6758 {where_clause} 

6759 {order_clause} 

6760 LIMIT ${param_count + 1} OFFSET ${param_count + 2} 

6761 ) 

6762 SELECT p.*, t._total_count 

6763 FROM total t 

6764 LEFT JOIN paged p ON true 

6765 ORDER BY p.{sort_field} {sort_direction.upper()} NULLS LAST 

6766 """ 

6767 query_timing_label = f"{self.workspace} PGDocStatusStorage.get_docs_paginated" 

6768 result = await self.db.query( 

6769 cte_sql, 

6770 list(params.values()), 

6771 True, 

6772 timing_label=query_timing_label, 

6773 ) 

6774 total_count = result[0]["_total_count"] if result else 0 

6775 

6776 # Convert to (doc_id, DocProcessingStatus) tuples 

6777 documents = [] 

6778 for element in result: 

6779 if element["id"] is None: 

6780 # Empty-page sentinel row from LEFT JOIN when paged has no rows. 

6781 continue 

6782 doc_id = element["id"] 

6783 

6784 # Parse metadata JSON string back to dict 

6785 metadata = element.get("metadata", {}) 

6786 if isinstance(metadata, str): 

6787 try: 

6788 metadata = json.loads(metadata) 

6789 except json.JSONDecodeError: 

6790 metadata = {} 

6791 

6792 # Convert datetime objects to ISO format strings with timezone info 

6793 created_at = self._format_datetime_with_timezone(element["created_at"]) 

6794 updated_at = self._format_datetime_with_timezone(element["updated_at"]) 

6795 

6796 doc_status = DocProcessingStatus( 

6797 content_summary=element["content_summary"], 

6798 content_length=element["content_length"], 

6799 status=element["status"], 

6800 created_at=created_at, 

6801 updated_at=updated_at, 

6802 chunks_count=element["chunks_count"], 

6803 file_path=element["file_path"], 

6804 chunks_list=[], # not fetched: unused by pagination response 

6805 track_id=element.get("track_id"), 

6806 metadata=metadata, 

6807 error_msg=element.get("error_msg"), 

6808 content_hash=element.get("content_hash"), 

6809 ) 

6810 documents.append((doc_id, doc_status)) 

6811 

6812 elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start 

6813 performance_timing_log( 

6814 "[%s] PGDocStatusStorage.get_docs_paginated completed in %.4fs returned_rows=%s total_count=%s status_filter=%s page=%s page_size=%s sort_field=%s sort_direction=%s", 

6815 self.workspace, 

6816 elapsed, 

6817 len(documents), 

6818 total_count, 

6819 status_filter_value, 

6820 page, 

6821 page_size, 

6822 sort_field, 

6823 sort_direction, 

6824 ) 

6825 

6826 return documents, total_count

7154class PGGraphEdgeWriteLostError(PGGraphQueryException): 

7155 """Raised when an edge upsert completed without writing an edge. 

7156 

7157 The AGE upsert Cypher is ``MATCH (source) ... MATCH (target) ... CREATE``: 

7158 if either endpoint is absent the whole pattern fails to match, the statement 

7159 succeeds with zero rows, and the relation is dropped on the floor. Every 

7160 in-tree caller creates its endpoints first (``merge_nodes_and_edges``, 

7161 ``ainsert_custom_kg``, the graph-edit flows in ``utils_graph``), so this can 

7162 only fire on a real defect or a concurrent endpoint deletion — cases where a 

7163 silent drop is far worse than an error. 

7164 

7165 Attributes: 

7166 source_node_id / target_node_id: the endpoints of the lost edge. 

7167 missing_endpoints: the endpoint ids found absent, when identifiable. 

7168 """ 

7169 

7170 def __init__( 

7171 self, 

7172 graph_name: str, 

7173 source_node_id: str, 

7174 target_node_id: str, 

7175 missing_endpoints: Sequence[str] = (), 

7176 ) -> None: 

7177 self.graph_name = graph_name 

7178 self.source_node_id = source_node_id 

7179 self.target_node_id = target_node_id 

7180 self.missing_endpoints = tuple(missing_endpoints) 

7181 if self.missing_endpoints: 

7182 details = "missing endpoint node(s): " + ", ".join( 

7183 f"`{node_id}`" for node_id in self.missing_endpoints 

7184 ) 

7185 else: 

7186 details = ( 

7187 "both endpoints appear to exist; the edge write was most likely " 

7188 "lost to a concurrent endpoint deletion" 

7189 ) 

7190 message = ( 

7191 f"PostgreSQL AGE: edge `{source_node_id}`-`{target_node_id}` was not " 

7192 f"written to graph {graph_name} ({details})" 

7193 ) 

7194 super().__init__({"message": message, "details": details}) 

7195 # PGGraphQueryException does not populate Exception.args, which would 

7196 # make str(exc) empty in logs and test output. 

7197 self.args = (message,) 

7198 

7199 

7200def _is_transient_graph_write_error(exc: BaseException) -> bool: 

7201 """Return True when a PGGraphQueryException wraps a transient write-time error. 

7202 

7203 The inner _run_with_retry already handles connection-level transient errors 

7204 (pool reset, TCP failures, etc.). This predicate covers query-level transient 

7205 errors that survive the connection layer and surface as PGGraphQueryException: 

7206 deadlocks, serialization conflicts, and lock-acquisition timeouts that can 

7207 occur under concurrent document ingestion. 

7208 """ 

7209 if not isinstance(exc, PGGraphQueryException): 

7210 return False 

7211 cause = exc.__cause__ 

7212 if cause is None: 

7213 return False 

7214 return isinstance( 

7215 cause, 

7216 ( 

7217 asyncpg.exceptions.DeadlockDetectedError, 

7218 asyncpg.exceptions.SerializationError, 

7219 asyncpg.exceptions.LockNotAvailableError, 

7220 asyncpg.exceptions.QueryCanceledError, 

7221 ), 

7222 ) 

7223 

7224 

7225# Transaction-scoped advisory lock that serialises concurrent upserts of the 

7226# *same logical edge* (single-row ``upsert_edge``). Keyed on 

7227# (graph_name, ordered (src, tgt)) so {A,B}/{B,A} collide while the same pair in 

7228# a different graph/workspace does not. It is the DB-level last line of defense 

7229# for the busy-check race on the graph-edit endpoints (see 

7230# document_routes.check_pipeline_busy_or_raise): two concurrent writers could 

7231# otherwise both pass the OPTIONAL MATCH and both CREATE, leaving duplicate 

7232# DIRECTED rows. 

7233_EDGE_ADVISORY_LOCK_SQL = ( 

7234 "SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(" 

7235 " hashtextextended(" 

7236 " $1::text || E'\\x01' ||" 

7237 " LEAST($2::text, $3::text) || E'\\x01' || GREATEST($2::text, $3::text)," 

7238 " 0" 

7239 " )" 

7240 ")" 

7241) 

7242 

7243# Graph-wide advisory locks keyed on the whole graph ($1 = graph_name), used so 

7244# the edge *batch* path conflicts with concurrent single-edge writers without 

7245# taking one lock per edge. 

7246# 

7247# * EXCLUSIVE (batch): one ``pg_advisory_xact_lock`` per chunk -- a single 

7248# advisory lock regardless of edge count, so it can't pile up to the chunk 

7249# size or exhaust the shared lock table. It serialises a bulk edge write 

7250# against the graph as one unit. 

7251# * SHARED (single): every single ``upsert_edge`` also takes 

7252# ``pg_advisory_xact_lock_shared`` on the same key. Shared/shared is 

7253# compatible, so concurrent single-edge writes on *different* edges do not 

7254# serialise (pipeline concurrency preserved); shared/exclusive conflicts, so 

7255# a batch and any single-edge writer on the same graph cannot interleave 

7256# their OPTIONAL MATCH/DELETE/CREATE and create duplicate DIRECTED rows. 

7257# 

7258# The shared graph lock does NOT serialise two single writers of the *same* 

7259# edge (shared/shared is compatible) -- that is what the per-edge 

7260# ``_EDGE_ADVISORY_LOCK_SQL`` is for; the two cover different races. 

7261_GRAPH_ADVISORY_LOCK_SQL = "SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended($1::text, 0))" 

7262_GRAPH_ADVISORY_LOCK_SHARED_SQL = ( 

7263 "SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock_shared(hashtextextended($1::text, 0))" 

7264)

7284 def _get_workspace_graph_name(self) -> str: 

7285 """ 

7286 Generate graph name based on workspace and namespace for data isolation. 

7287 Rules: 

7288 - If workspace is empty or "default": graph_name = namespace 

7289 - If workspace has other value: graph_name = workspace_namespace 

7290 

7291 Args: 

7292 None 

7293 

7294 Returns: 

7295 str: The graph name for the current workspace 

7296 """ 

7297 workspace = self.workspace 

7298 namespace = self.namespace 

7299 

7300 if workspace and workspace.strip() and workspace.strip().lower() != "default": 7300 ↛ 7307line 7300 didn't jump to line 7307 because the condition on line 7300 was always true

7301 # Ensure names comply with PostgreSQL identifier specifications 

7302 safe_workspace = re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9_]", "_", workspace.strip()) 

7303 safe_namespace = re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9_]", "_", namespace) 

7304 return f"{safe_workspace}_{safe_namespace}"

7309 @staticmethod 

7310 def _normalize_node_id(node_id: str) -> str: 

7311 """ 

7312 Normalize node ID to ensure special characters are properly handled in Cypher queries. 

7313 

7314 Used by write paths that still embed entity IDs in Cypher strings 

7315 (delete_node, remove_nodes, remove_edges). The upsert paths now use 

7316 parameterized Cypher instead. 

7317 

7318 Within a Cypher double-quoted string the only recognised escape 

7319 sequences are ``\\"`` and ``\\\\``. We also strip null bytes which 

7320 could truncate the string in some PostgreSQL/AGE code paths. 

7321 

7322 Args: 

7323 node_id: The original node ID 

7324 

7325 Returns: 

7326 Normalized node ID suitable for embedding in a Cypher double-quoted string 

7327 """ 

7328 # Strip null bytes that could truncate the string 

7329 normalized_id = node_id.replace("\x00", "") 

7330 # Escape backslashes first (order matters) 

7331 normalized_id = normalized_id.replace("\\", "\\\\") 

7332 # Escape double quotes 

7333 normalized_id = normalized_id.replace('"', '\\"') 

7334 return normalized_id

7367 # is handled safely (unlike a bare pool.acquire() call). 

7368 async def _do_configure_age_extension( 

7369 connection: asyncpg.Connection, 

7370 ) -> None:

7372 

7373 await self.db._run_with_retry(_do_configure_age_extension)

7375 # Only create the labels that are actually missing. create_vlabel / 

7376 # create_elabel have no IF NOT EXISTS form, so calling them for an 

7377 # existing label makes PostgreSQL log an ERROR on every startup 

7378 # with_age=True here also guarantees the graph 

7379 # itself exists before we read its labels. 

7380 existing_labels = await self.db.query( 

7381 "SELECT l.name::text AS name " 

7382 "FROM ag_catalog.ag_label l " 

7383 "JOIN ag_catalog.ag_graph g ON l.graph = g.graphid " 

7384 f"WHERE g.name = left($1, {_PG_NAME_MAX_BYTES})::name", 

7385 [self.graph_name], 

7386 multirows=True, 

7387 with_age=True, 

7388 graph_name=self.graph_name, 

7389 ) 

7390 present_labels = {row["name"] for row in existing_labels or []} 

7391 

7392 # Execute each statement separately and ignore errors. 

7393 # 

7394 # create_graph() is deliberately absent: every statement below runs 

7395 # with with_age=True, and the first one to do so has already had 

7396 # PostgreSQLDB._ensure_age_graph() create the graph. Repeating it 

7397 # here would only add one more "graph already exists" line to the 

7398 # PostgreSQL log.

7400 # The index statements carry IF NOT EXISTS for the same reason: a 

7401 # plain CREATE INDEX on an existing index is an ERROR the server 

7402 # logs before the client can ignore it, while IF NOT EXISTS 

7403 # downgrades it to a NOTICE that never reaches the log. 

7404 queries = [ 

7405 *( 

7406 [f"SELECT create_vlabel('{self.graph_name}', 'base');"] 

7407 if "base" not in present_labels 

7408 else [] 

7409 ), 

7410 *( 

7411 [f"SELECT create_elabel('{self.graph_name}', 'DIRECTED');"] 

7412 if "DIRECTED" not in present_labels 

7413 else [] 

7414 ), 

7415 # f'CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS vertex_p_idx ON {self.graph_name}."_ag_label_vertex" (id)', 

7416 f'CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS vertex_idx_node_id ON {self.graph_name}."_ag_label_vertex" (ag_catalog.agtype_access_operator(properties, \'"entity_id"\'::agtype))', 

7417 # f'CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS edge_p_idx ON {self.graph_name}."_ag_label_edge" (id)', 

7418 f'CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS edge_sid_idx ON {self.graph_name}."_ag_label_edge" (start_id)', 

7419 f'CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS edge_eid_idx ON {self.graph_name}."_ag_label_edge" (end_id)', 

7420 f'CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS edge_seid_idx ON {self.graph_name}."_ag_label_edge" (start_id,end_id)', 

7421 f'CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS directed_p_idx ON {self.graph_name}."DIRECTED" (id)', 

7422 f'CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS directed_eid_idx ON {self.graph_name}."DIRECTED" (end_id)', 

7423 f'CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS directed_sid_idx ON {self.graph_name}."DIRECTED" (start_id)', 

7424 f'CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS directed_seid_idx ON {self.graph_name}."DIRECTED" (start_id,end_id)', 

7425 f'CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS entity_p_idx ON {self.graph_name}."base" (id)', 

7426 f'CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS entity_idx_node_id ON {self.graph_name}."base" (ag_catalog.agtype_access_operator(properties, \'"entity_id"\'::agtype))', 

7427 f'CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS entity_node_id_gin_idx ON {self.graph_name}."base" using gin(properties)', 

7428 f'ALTER TABLE {self.graph_name}."DIRECTED" CLUSTER ON directed_sid_idx', 

7429 ] 

7430 

7431 for query in queries: 

7432 # Use the new flag to silently ignore "already exists" errors 

7433 # at the source, preventing log spam. 

7434 await self.db.execute( 

7435 query, 

7436 upsert=True, 

7437 ignore_if_exists=True, # Pass the new flag 

7438 with_age=True, 

7439 graph_name=self.graph_name, 

7440 )

7451 @staticmethod 

7452 def _record_to_dict(record: asyncpg.Record) -> dict[str, Any]: 

7453 """ 

7454 Convert a record returned from an age query to a dictionary 

7455 

7456 Args: 

7457 record (): a record from an age query result 

7458 

7459 Returns: 

7460 dict[str, Any]: a dictionary representation of the record where 

7461 the dictionary key is the field name and the value is the 

7462 value converted to a python type 

7463 """ 

7464 

7465 @staticmethod 

7466 def parse_agtype_string(agtype_str: str) -> tuple[str, str]: 

7467 """ 

7468 Parse agtype string precisely, separating JSON content and type identifier 

7469 

7470 Args: 

7471 agtype_str: String like '{"json": "content"}::vertex' 

7472 

7473 Returns: 

7474 (json_content, type_identifier) 

7475 """ 

7476 if not isinstance(agtype_str, str) or "::" not in agtype_str: 

7477 return agtype_str, "" 

7478 

7479 # Find the last :: from the right, which is the start of type identifier 

7480 last_double_colon = agtype_str.rfind("::") 

7481 

7482 if last_double_colon == -1: 

7483 return agtype_str, "" 

7484 

7485 # Separate JSON content and type identifier 

7486 json_content = agtype_str[:last_double_colon] 

7487 type_identifier = agtype_str[last_double_colon + 2 :] 

7488 

7489 return json_content, type_identifier 

7490 

7491 @staticmethod 

7492 def safe_json_parse(json_str: str, context: str = "") -> dict: 

7493 """ 

7494 Safe JSON parsing with simplified error logging 

7495 """ 

7496 try: 

7497 return json.loads(json_str) 

7498 except json.JSONDecodeError as e: 

7499 logger.error(f"JSON parsing failed ({context}): {e}") 

7500 logger.error(f"Raw data (first 100 chars): {repr(json_str[:100])}") 

7501 logger.error(f"Error position: line {e.lineno}, column {e.colno}") 

7502 return None 

7503 

7504 # result holder 

7505 d = {} 

7506 

7507 # prebuild a mapping of vertex_id to vertex mappings to be used 

7508 # later to build edges 

7509 vertices = {} 

7510 

7511 # First pass: preprocess vertices 

7512 for k in record.keys(): 

7513 v = record[k] 

7514 if isinstance(v, str) and "::" in v: 

7515 if v.startswith("[") and v.endswith("]"): 

7516 # Handle vertex arrays 

7517 json_content, type_id = parse_agtype_string(v) 

7518 if type_id == "vertex": 

7519 vertexes = safe_json_parse( 

7520 json_content, f"vertices array for {k}" 

7521 ) 

7522 if vertexes: 

7523 for vertex in vertexes: 

7524 vertices[vertex["id"]] = vertex.get("properties") 

7525 else: 

7526 # Handle single vertex 

7527 json_content, type_id = parse_agtype_string(v) 

7528 if type_id == "vertex": 

7529 vertex = safe_json_parse(json_content, f"single vertex for {k}") 

7530 if vertex: 

7531 vertices[vertex["id"]] = vertex.get("properties") 

7532 

7533 # Second pass: process all fields 

7534 for k in record.keys(): 

7535 v = record[k] 

7536 if isinstance(v, str) and "::" in v: 

7537 if v.startswith("[") and v.endswith("]"): 

7538 # Handle array types 

7539 json_content, type_id = parse_agtype_string(v) 

7540 if type_id in ["vertex", "edge"]: 

7541 parsed_data = safe_json_parse( 

7542 json_content, f"array {type_id} for field {k}" 

7543 ) 

7544 d[k] = parsed_data if parsed_data is not None else None 

7545 else: 

7546 logger.warning(f"Unknown array type: {type_id}") 

7547 d[k] = None 

7548 else: 

7549 # Handle single objects 

7550 json_content, type_id = parse_agtype_string(v) 

7551 if type_id in ["vertex", "edge"]: 

7552 parsed_data = safe_json_parse( 

7553 json_content, f"single {type_id} for field {k}" 

7554 ) 

7555 d[k] = parsed_data if parsed_data is not None else None 

7556 else: 

7557 # May be other types of agtype data, keep as is 

7558 d[k] = v 

7559 else: 

7560 d[k] = v # Keep as string 

7561 

7562 return d 

7563 

7564 @staticmethod 

7565 def _format_properties( 

7566 properties: dict[str, Any], _id: Union[str, None] = None 

7567 ) -> str: 

7568 """ 

7569 Convert a dictionary of properties to a string representation that 

7570 can be used in a cypher query insert/merge statement. 

7571 

7572 Args: 

7573 properties (dict[str,str]): a dictionary containing node/edge properties 

7574 _id (Union[str, None]): the id of the node or None if none exists

7576 Returns: 

7577 str: the properties dictionary as a properly formatted string

7579 props = [] 

7580 # Wrap property keys in backticks and escape embedded backticks to 

7581 # preserve the Cypher structure when property names contain specials. 

7582 for k, v in properties.items(): 

7583 safe_key = str(k).replace("`", "``") 

7584 prop = f"`{safe_key}`: {json.dumps(v, ensure_ascii=False)}" 

7585 props.append(prop) 

7586 if _id is not None and "id" not in properties: 7586 ↛ 7587line 7586 didn't jump to line 7587 because the condition on line 7586 was never true

7587 props.append( 

7588 f"id: {json.dumps(_id, ensure_ascii=False)}" 

7589 if isinstance(_id, str) 

7590 else f"id: {_id}" 

7591 ) 

7592 return "{" + ", ".join(props) + "}"

7670 async def has_node(self, node_id: str) -> bool: 

7671 query = f""" 

7672 SELECT EXISTS ( 

7673 SELECT 1 

7674 FROM {self.graph_name}.base 

7675 WHERE ag_catalog.agtype_access_operator( 

7676 VARIADIC ARRAY[properties, '"entity_id"'::agtype] 

7677 ) = (to_json($1::text)::text)::agtype 

7678 LIMIT 1 

7679 ) AS node_exists; 

7680 """ 

7681 

7682 params = {"node_id": node_id} 

7683 row = (await self._query(query, params=params))[0] 

7684 return bool(row["node_exists"])

7690 FROM {self.graph_name}.base 

7691 WHERE ag_catalog.agtype_access_operator( 

7692 VARIADIC ARRAY[properties, '"entity_id"'::agtype] 

7693 ) = (to_json($1::text)::text)::agtype 

7694 ), 

7695 b AS (

7697 FROM {self.graph_name}.base 

7698 WHERE ag_catalog.agtype_access_operator( 

7699 VARIADIC ARRAY[properties, '"entity_id"'::agtype] 

7700 ) = (to_json($2::text)::text)::agtype 

7701 ) 

7702 SELECT EXISTS ( 

7703 SELECT 1 

7704 FROM {self.graph_name}."DIRECTED" d 

7705 JOIN a ON d.start_id = a.vid 

7706 JOIN b ON d.end_id = b.vid

7708 ) 

7709 OR EXISTS ( 

7710 SELECT 1 

7711 FROM {self.graph_name}."DIRECTED" d

7714 LIMIT 1

7716 """

7718 "source_node_id": source_node_id,

7720 }
